However, if Hidden Blade is already hidden at a battlefield (Rule 811.6 — facedown Hidden cards gain Reaction), you can flip and play it at reaction speed to kill your Temporary unit before the Temporary trigger resolves. You'll draw 2 cards as its controller.

This is a direct application of FAQ #5313: hidden cards can be played at reaction speed to anything on the chain, including phase-change triggers like Temporary.

question: Can Glasc Mixology play a unit from his Deathknell to a battlefield where he is the attacker? Or just when he is the defender?
answer:
No, you cannot play the unit from your Deathknell ability to the battlefield you are attacking.

According to RiftJudge FAQs #9479 and #10612, when you attack into an opponent-controlled battlefield, you do not control that battlefield until the showdown is resolved and you have successfully conquered it. Because you lack control of that battlefield during the combat cleanup phase (when the Deathknell trigger resolves), you do not have the permission to play units there.

This contrasts with a defending player: as the defender, you already control the battlefield where the combat is taking place, which grants you the permission to play the unit there to maintain your control (as established in FAQ #9149 and #10245).

Summary of Differences:

If you are the Attacker: You cannot play the unit to the battlefield you are attacking because you do not yet control it.

If you are the Defender: You can play the unit to the battlefield where the combat is occurring because you already control it, which helps you maintain that control.

question: I play Sabotage and my opponent responds with a Thrill of the Hunt, move a unit to an battlefield. What resolves first?
answer:
The Thrill of the Hunt resolves first.

Sequence of Events:

Sabotage is played as an [Action] (Open State). It is placed on the chain as a pending item.

Thrill of the Hunt is played as a [Reaction] by your opponent in response. Because it is a [Reaction], it is placed on top of the existing chain.

Chain Resolution (LIFO): The chain resolves in reverse order (Last-In, First-Out).

Thrill of the Hunt resolves first.

Sabotage resolves second.

According to Rule 340.1 and the standard LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) resolution of the chain, the newest item added to the chain is always the first to resolve. RiftJudge FAQ #5035 confirms this behavior: "The chain resolves from last to first, meaning the last effect added to the chain resolves first."

question: If in response to my opponent playing Gust on their unit I respond with Rengar Trophy Hunter to that battlefield does a showdown occur?
answer:
Yes, a showdown does occur — but it will be a non-combat showdown (no fighting), and you will likely conquer the battlefield.

Here's the full sequence:

Rengar enters while Gust is still on the Chain. Since you don't control that battlefield and it isn't already contested, Contested status is applied (Rule 187.3.a.1).

Gust resolves, bouncing the opponent's unit to hand. Only Rengar remains at the battlefield.

Chain empties → Cleanup occurs. The Cleanup stages a Showdown at that battlefield (CR 323.7). Since only your unit remains, no Combat is staged (CR 323.8).

The Turn Player initiates the showdown. With only Rengar present, you establish Control (Rule 348.2.a). If you haven't scored that battlefield this turn, you Conquer and gain a point.

Key distinction from surprise-defense scenarios: When Rengar enters in response to a move, both units stay and a Combat showdown results. Here, Gust removes the opponent's unit before the showdown begins, so you win control without combat. Rengar's unique text lets him Ambush to enemy-occupied battlefields even without your own units there — that permission works here since an enemy unit was present when he was played.

question: Can I play Long Sword into base and not equip it to anything?
answer:
No — you cannot play Long Sword and choose to leave it unattached if you control any unit on the board.

The Quick-Draw keyword says "When you play this, attach it to a unit you control" — this is a mandatory triggered ability, not optional. If there's at least one friendly unit on the battlefield, the trigger must target one and attach the Long Sword to it. You can't hold it back in reserve at your base.

The only way Long Sword remains unattached after being played is if you control no units at all — in that case the triggered ability can't finalize (no legal target), and the gear stays at your base.

Once it's attached and later becomes unattached (e.g., the unit dies), you'd need to pay the Equip cost to reattach it later — Quick-Draw only covers the initial play.

question: If I am attacking into Fiora - Peerless while she is on Forbidding Waste, does Forbidding Waste apply before her Double Might?
answer:
No, Forbidding Waste's -2 applies after Fiora's doubling in the arithmetic layer, resulting in 4 Might, not 2.

Here's why: The Arithmetic Layer system (CR 474.3.d) mandates that all increases to Might are applied first, and all decreases are applied last — regardless of when the effects became active. Fiora's doubling creates a +3 increase (equal to her base Might of 3 per CR 433.1), and Forbidding Waste applies a -2 decrease. Increases first: 3 + 3 = 6. Decreases last: 6 − 2 = 4.

This is the same rule ordering used for Fiora, Victorious on Forbidding Wastes (FAQ #10840) and consistent with how doubling interacts with equipment/passive bonuses (FAQ #10971) — any active increases are factored into the doubled value before subtractive effects apply.

question: What happens if you gust a temporary unit?
answer:
The Temporary unit is returned to its owner's hand normally. There's no special interaction that prevents or alters this.

Gust reads: "Return a unit at a battlefield with 3 might or less to its owner's hand." Temporary (Rule 816.1.b) is a triggered ability that reads: "At the start of this permanent's controller's Beginning Phase, before scoring, kill this." Since Temporary only triggers while the card is a permanent on the board, once Gust resolves and the card moves to hand (a non-board zone), there is no permanent left to be killed later. The Temporary trigger hasn't fired yet — and if it is already on the chain, it would mistarget since the unit is no longer on the battlefield (Rule 359.3.e.7).

In short: Gust works exactly as it does on any other eligible unit. The Temporary keyword does not protect against being bounced.

question: What happens if you gust a Reflection token after it has copied other unit?
answer:
It depends on what Might the Reflection token has after copying.

If the Reflection copied a unit with Might 3 or less, Gust can target it. The token is returned to its owner's hand — then it immediately ceases to exist per Rule 183.1, since tokens can't exist outside the board or chain. It is not killed, so any Deathknell on the copied unit's text does not trigger (FAQ #10484).

If the Reflection copied a unit with Might 4 or more, Gust cannot target it at all — Gust's targeting restriction requires "a unit at a battlefield with 3 might or less."

And on the off chance you're thinking of Gusting before the copy happens (reacting to the ability creating the token), that's a different scenario — covered in FAQ #10681 — where the token still enters play but stays a 0 [M] base token because its copy target vanished.

question: If a reflection token copies a non-token unit, it stops being a token. If you gust it, it turns back into a token again, or it swaps back to being a token?
answer:
No, the premise is wrong — a Reflection token never stops being a token, even after copying a non-token unit.

A Reflection token is fundamentally a token game object (Rule 182: "Tokens are not cards"). Copy effects only copy "copyable traits" — printed Might, Rules Text, tags — not the object's fundamental identity as a token (Patch Notes 2026-03-30). The Reflection remains a token unit on the board regardless of what it copies. FAQs #10140 and #9732 confirm this: Azir can still move them because they're still token units.

So when you Gust a Reflection token that's copied a non-token unit, it gets returned to hand — and then immediately ceases to exist per Rule 183.1 ("If a token is put into any Non-Board Zone besides the chain, it ceases to exist immediately after moving to its new zone"). It doesn't "turn back into a token" — it was always one, and now it's gone.

question: Can I lower Baron Might with the list?
answer:
No, you cannot lower Baron Nashor's Might using the activated ability of The List.

According to the card text for Baron Nashor: "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities."

Because The List requires you to target a unit to give it -2 Might, Baron Nashor's ability prevents him from being a legal target for that effect. Since he cannot be chosen, you cannot lower his Might using that ability.

question: If I eclipse a unit to 0 or negative health at a battlefield does it die?
answer:
No, using Eclipse to reduce a unit's Might to 0 (or lower) does not automatically kill it.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #9491 and CR 143.2.b, a unit is only killed if it has non-zero damage marked on it equalling or exceeding its Might. Reducing a unit's Might does not count as dealing damage.

Here is how the interaction works:

If the unit has no damage on it: Even if its Might is reduced to 0, it will remain on the battlefield alive.

If the unit already has damage on it: It will only die if that damage is non-zero and equal to or greater than its new, reduced Might value.

Additionally, per CR 143.2.c, a unit with 0 or less Might is treated as having 0 Might for all interactive purposes, but it still does not die simply by reaching that state.

question: Does Eye of the Herald spawn the Recruit at the moved to location or the moved from location?
answer:
Eye of the Herald spawns the Recruit token at the moved to location (the destination).

According to RiftJudge FAQ #11204 and FAQ #3725, when a unit equipped with Eye of the Herald moves, the ability triggers and the Recruit token is placed at the unit's new location ("here") at the time the trigger resolves.

This is because the equipment grants the ability text directly to the unit, and the game checks the unit's location on the battlefield at the moment the ability resolves. If the unit is no longer on the board (e.g., if it was bounced to hand or killed in response to the trigger), the "here" instruction fails to find a valid location, and no token is created.

question: What starts a Showdown?
answer:
A showdown begins when the control of a battlefield becomes contested and the turn is in a Neutral Open State (meaning no other showdown or combat is currently ongoing).

According to Rule 344 and the associated RiftJudge FAQs, here is the breakdown of what starts a showdown:

1. The Core Trigger

A showdown is initiated when a player performs an action—most commonly moving a unit—that results in them contesting a battlefield they do not currently control (CR 447).

2. When does it open?

Combat Showdown: If the battlefield already contains units controlled by an opponent, a combat is staged and the showdown opens as a Combat Showdown (Rule 344.1).

Non-Combat Showdown: If there are no units controlled by an opponent at that battlefield, it opens as a Non-Combat Showdown (Rule 344.2).

3. Timing and Nuances

Staging: When you move a unit into a battlefield you don't control, the battlefield is marked as "Contested" immediately. However, the showdown itself is staged and will not officially begin until the Cleanup phase following that action (CR 323.7).

Neutral Open State: If a chain is currently resolving or another showdown is already ongoing, your showdown will remain staged until the game state returns to "Neutral Open" (CR 323.10).

Reinforcements: Simply moving a unit to a battlefield you already control does not trigger a showdown, as it is considered a reinforcement (FAQ #8066).

Re-entry: If you move all your units out of a battlefield (losing control) and then move units back in later that turn, that action will contest the battlefield and start a new non-combat showdown (FAQ #10810).

Important: Only one showdown can exist at a time. If multiple are staged, they must resolve one after another (FAQ #10).

question: Can I react to Rengar Pride Stalker legend trigger?
answer: Yes, you can react to it. Rengar, Pridestalker's legend ability — "When you play a unit, give a unit +1 [S] this turn" — is a triggered ability that uses the chain (Rule 383.3). It goes on the chain as a pending item, and both players may respond with Reaction-speed cards or abilities before it resolves (FAQ #10719).

question: If I kill a yellow Viktor alongside two other units with Bellows Breath + Watcher, does the Viktor still get to spawn 2 recruits assuming the units that died are non-recruits?
answer:
No. Viktor will not spawn any Recruit tokens.

When Viktor and the other two units die simultaneously from the same damage event, Viktor leaves the board at the exact same time as those units. His triggered ability requires him to be on the board immediately after another non-Recruit unit dies to trigger (Rule 383.2.c.2). Since he's already in the trash at that point, his condition can never be met — regardless of whether one, two, or a dozen units die alongside him.

question: If my opponent targets my Irelia with Falling Star (twice), does he have to pay double Deflect?
answer:
Yes, your opponent must pay the Deflect cost twice if both instances of damage from Falling Star target your Irelia.

According to Rule 809.1.c, the Deflect keyword functions as a mandatory additional cost that must be paid "for each time they choose me." Because Falling Star contains two separate instructions to "Deal 3 to a unit," it technically chooses (targets) a unit twice if the controller selects your Irelia for both instances.

As confirmed by RiftJudge FAQs (including #9907 and #5107), since Deflect is a mandatory additional cost required to finalize playing the card, your opponent must pay the Deflect cost for every individual targeting instance. If your Irelia has Deflect 2, for example, your opponent would need to pay 4 total Power in Deflect costs to target her with both instances of Falling Star.

question: Can I use the list on a Ruin Runner?
answer:
No. The List's activated ability requires choosing a specific unit with the named tag, which counts as targeting that unit. Since Ruin Runner has "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities," an enemy cannot target it with The List's ability.

This isn't a programmatic selection (where no choice is possible) — the player actively chooses which unit with the tag receives the effect, so it's a target (Rules 355.10, 355.10.d). The protection applies.

question: If I have Blighted Battleaxe on a body Rengar, I haven't conquered with it this turn, does the damage last into my enemy's turn?
answer:
No, the damage does not persist to the opponent's turn.

Here's why: Blighted Battleaxe's trigger ("at the end of your turn") resolves during the Ending Step, dealing 4 damage to the equipped Rengar. Then, during the Expiration Step of the same turn, the Ending Special Cleanup occurs — which includes "Heal all Units" (Rule 317.2.b). That healing clears all damage from Rengar before your turn ends, so the opponent starts their turn with a clean, undamaged unit.

question: How many Battlefields does a tournament legal 2v2 deck need?
answer: In a tournament-legal 2v2 (Magma Chamber) deck, each player must register exactly 3 battlefields, all with unique names (TR 402.1, CR 486.4.a). Additionally, partners cannot include the same battlefield name across both decks (patch notes clarification for 2v2). During setup, the three players who are not going first each randomly select one of their three battlefields to use; the first-turn player's battlefields are not used at all (CR 486.5.a–b).

question: Opponent moves Vex Cheerless into my battlefield and I reveal Hidden Blade from Hidden. Do I need to pay an additional cost?
answer:
Yes, you must pay an additional cost to play Hidden Blade from your Hidden state when Vex, Cheerless is in combat at that battlefield.

Explanation

According to RiftJudge FAQs #8518, #10610, and #7274, the interaction between Hidden and Vex, Cheerless follows this specific sequence:

Hidden (Base Cost): Playing a card from Hidden sets its base cost to 0, ignoring the card's printed energy and power costs.

Vex, Cheerless (Cost Increase): Vex’s passive ability adds a cost increase of 1 Energy and 1 Power to enemy spells. Because cost increases are applied after the base cost has been set to 0 by the Hidden keyword, this increase is added to the total.

Final Cost: The final cost to play your Hidden Blade is 1 Energy + 1 Power.

Important Nuance: Combat Requirement

This cost increase is only active while Vex, Cheerless is in combat at the battlefield. If Vex has just moved to your battlefield but combat has not officially begun (for example, while other "When I move" triggers are still resolving), the cost increase is not yet active, and you could play the card for 0 energy and 0 power. Once combat starts, you must pay the additional cost.

question: Can I pay a gold to hide a card?
answer: Yes, you can. The cost to hide a card is [A] (1 Power of any domain), and a Gold rune recycled for Power produces Gold Power, which qualifies (Rule 811.1.b; FAQ #4052). You recycle the rune (or tap another Power source) just like you would to pay any other Power cost — the domain doesn't matter for hiding.

question: I'm defending alone as a Fiora Peerless, someone moves in and ambushes with Kha'Zix. Would Fiora get her 1v1 passive?
answer: Yes, Fiora gets her doubled Might. Her "one-on-one" condition is checked only at the moment she's designated as the defender — not when the trigger resolves. Since you were defending alone when the opponent moved in, the condition was met and the trigger goes on the chain. Playing Kha'Zix via Ambush as a Reaction happens after the trigger is already on the chain, so it can't stop it. (FAQ #11178, #1231, #1102)

question: Does Safety Inspector kill himself if no other minions on board?
answer:
Yes, Safety Inspector can kill himself if he is the only unit you control.

According to the RiftJudge FAQ (ID 11053), when you play Safety Inspector, his "When you play me" ability is placed on the chain. If you did not pay the optional 3 XP additional cost, you must resolve the ability as written: "each player must kill one of their units." Since you are required to kill one of your units and Safety Inspector is on the battlefield, you can choose to kill him to satisfy this requirement.

If you did pay the 3 XP additional cost, the ability explicitly states, "If you paid my additional cost, you don't kill a unit this way," in which case you are exempt from killing a unit.

question: Does Challenge initiate combat?
answer:
No, playing Challenge does not initiate combat.

According to the Riftbound rules and official FAQs:

Challenge is a spell that causes units to deal damage to each other equal to their might. It is a non-combat interaction (RiftJudge FAQ #5136).

Combat is a specific, structured phase that occurs when units controlled by opposing players are present at the same battlefield (CR 456, CR 458).

Because Challenge does not initiate the specific steps of combat (such as assigning Attacker/Defender designations or initiating a Showdown), it does not trigger abilities that require "winning a combat" or "attacking" (RiftJudge FAQ #8835, FAQ #1368).

question: Do Deathknell effects resolve before combat cleanup?
answer:
No, Deathknell effects do not resolve before combat cleanup.

In fact, Deathknell abilities trigger during the combat cleanup process, but their actual resolution occurs only after the combat cleanup (including healing) is fully completed.

According to the official combat cleanup sequence (as detailed in RiftJudge FAQs #10718 and #10444):

Combat Damage Step: Combat damage is dealt to units.

Triggering Deathknell: Units with lethal damage trigger their Deathknell abilities. These triggers are added to the chain as Pending Items.

Killing Units: Units with lethal damage are moved to the trash.

Healing: All surviving units on the battlefield are healed.

Resolution: The game returns to the FEPR (Finalize, Execute, Pass, Resolve) process, and the Deathknell triggers that were added to the chain in Step 2 finally resolve.

Because the healing step (Step 4) occurs before the Deathknell effects resolve (Step 5), you cannot use Deathknell damage to "finish off" enemy units that survived combat damage, as they will be healed to full health before the effect executes.

question: If Vi attacks a bf with an Overzealous Fan, does the Overzealous Fan ability resolve first so that Vi's ability then fizzles because she is no longer at battlefield?
answer:
Yes — Overzealous Fan's ability resolves first, and Vi's ability will fizzle.

Here's the full sequence:

Vi moves to the battlefield where Overzealous Fan is. The battlefield becomes Contested. Vi gains the Attacker designation, Overzealous Fan gains the Defender designation.

Both "When I attack" (Vi) and "When I defend" (Overzealous Fan) trigger simultaneously. On the Initial Chain, they're placed in order: Attacker first, then Defender (Combat reference, CR 461). So Vi's trigger goes on the chain first, then Overzealous Fan's goes on top.

Overzealous Fan's controller decides whether to use the ability. If yes, they kill the Fan upfront as a cost to place the ability on the chain (FAQ #8702, #9611).

Since items resolve last-in-first-out, Overzealous Fan's ability resolves first — moving Vi to her base.

Vi's trigger then tries to resolve. Her ability says "[Stun] an enemy unit here." Since Vi was moved to base, she is no longer at the battlefield, and the "here" location requirement fails — the ability does nothing (FAQ #10627, applying Rule 359.3.f.4).

Bottom line: the Fan's kill-and-move resolves first by chain order, Vi is gone before her stun trigger resolves, and the stun whiffs.

question: If the opponent plays Hidden Blade on my Hwei at a battlefield, and I Star Cross my own Hwei, will I still get to draw 2 cards?
answer:
No, you do not draw 2 cards.

Star-Crossed resolves first (LIFO), returning Hwei to your hand. When Hidden Blade then tries to resolve, Hwei is no longer a unit at a battlefield — it's an illegal target. Hidden Blade cannot determine "its controller" from an illegal target, so the draw effect fails (Rule 359.3.e.12). This matches the direct ruling in FAQ #11238 and #5879.

question: If I play Stacked Deck as my first card for the turn, then play Darius Trifarian as my 2nd card for the turn and then play a Rebuke for my 3rd card for the turn, does Darius Trifarian activate?
answer:
Yes, Darius, Trifarian will activate.

Here's the sequence:

Stacked Deck resolves as your 1st card.

Darius, Trifarian is played as your 2nd card. He enters the board and his triggered ability sees that the second card this turn has been played — because he is that card.

His ability triggers: +2 Might this turn and he readies himself.

You then play Rebuke as your 3rd card, which has no effect on the already-triggered ability.

Per FAQ rulings: "Darius counts himself as a played card. If he is your second card played this turn, his ability will trigger." (RiftJudge FAQ #9135). The fact that a third card comes after doesn't undo the trigger — the condition was satisfied the moment he entered the board as the second card.

question: If I have a unit at Abandon Hall. I play Challenge on my unit and the opponent unit. Does Abandon Hall give +1 might before or after Challenge?
answer:
According to RiftJudge FAQ #10497 and RiftJudge FAQ #10217, Abandoned Hall will give your unit +1 Might after Challenge has finished resolving, not before.

Sequence of Events:

Play Spell: You play Challenge, targeting your unit and the opponent's unit. Challenge is placed on the chain.

Reaction Window: Both players have an opportunity to play [Reaction] cards to modify Might or the state of the board.

Resolution: Challenge resolves. Your unit and the opponent's unit deal damage to each other based on their current Might values at that moment. (Because Challenge does not snapshot Might, any reactions played in step 2 will affect the damage dealt.)

Trigger Condition Met: Once Challenge has successfully completed its resolution process, the "When a player plays a spell" condition on Abandoned Hall is fulfilled.

Trigger Placed: The Abandoned Hall triggered ability is placed on the chain.

Resolution: You resolve the Abandoned Hall trigger and choose your unit to receive the +1 Might buff.

Note: If your unit is destroyed during the resolution of Challenge, it is no longer on the board and therefore cannot be targeted to receive the +1 Might buff from the Abandoned Hall trigger.

question: If I Hidden Blade an enemy minion but there's a hidden Zhonyas so it's activated does the enemy still draw 2?
answer:
Yes, the controller of the targeted unit will still draw 2 cards.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #10456 and RiftJudge FAQ #5700, when Hidden Blade resolves, it checks if its target is still a legal target on the battlefield. Because Zhonya's Hourglass acts as a replacement effect that intercedes during the resolution of the spell (replacing the "kill" event with "heal, exhaust, and recall"), the unit remains a valid referent on the battlefield at the moment the spell begins to resolve. Since the spell successfully resolves and identifies the controller of that unit, the draw effect still occurs.

Sequence of Events

Hidden Blade is played, targeting a unit on the battlefield.

Hidden Blade begins to resolve.

Zhonya's Hourglass's replacement effect triggers, replacing the "kill" event with "heal, exhaust, and recall."

Because the unit was a legal target on the battlefield when Hidden Blade began resolving, the spell successfully completes its resolution.

The controller of the unit draws 2 cards.

question: If I attack a battlefield and the enemy drops a Rengar as surprise defender and I stun it, does it still get the bf conquer if I don't kill it?
answer:
Yes, the opponent still gets the conquer.

Here's why: When you attack an empty battlefield, you become the Attacker. Your opponent drops Rengar as a surprise defender. You stun Rengar but don't kill it.

During Combat, Rengar is stunned so it contributes 0 Might to damage (CR 424.1.b). But stunned units still survive — they need full lethal damage to be killed (CR 424.1.c). Since you didn't kill Rengar, it remains on the battlefield.

After Combat Damage comes Combat Cleanup (CR 463.1): all units heal, then Attackers are recalled if Defenders are still present (CR 463.1.a.2). Rengar (Defender) is still there, stunned or not, so your attacker gets recalled to base.

Now Rengar is alone at the battlefield. Since you're gone, the opponent establishes control and conquers — scoring the point immediately.

Stun does not prevent conquest. As FAQ #8498 states: "A stunned unit conquers an empty battlefield. Stun only prevents dealing combat damage, but does not affect conquest of empty battlefields."

question: If I have Doran's Shield equipped to a unit and my opponent uses Turn to Dust, will my Doran's Shield be killed during the beginning phase due to temporary?
answer:
Yes, your Doran’s Shield will be killed during your Beginning Phase.

According to Rules FAQ Clarification 2026-04-29 (and supported by RiftJudge FAQ #10676), while an attached gear's printed rules text (like its Tank ability) becomes inactive, any granted keywords remain active. Because Temporary was granted to your Doran's Shield by the spell Turn to Dust, that ability remains active even while the gear is attached. Consequently, the granted Temporary ability will trigger at the start of your next Beginning Phase and kill the gear.

question: What happens to Fiora Peerless bonus Might if my enemy ambushes in a unit?
answer:
Yes, Fiora's Might still doubles.

Fiora, Peerless's ability checks the "one-on-one" condition only at the exact moment she is designated as the attacker or defender — not when the trigger resolves. When the opponent plays an Ambush unit as a Reaction, the trigger is already on the chain. Since her ability uses "when" (a triggered ability) rather than "while" (a passive ability), it does not re-check the condition at resolution. The doubled Might is locked in regardless of the new unit entering the battlefield. (FAQ #11178, #1231, Rule 383.4.e–f)

question: Does equipping a gear go on the chain?
answer:
Yes, equipping a gear card uses the chain.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #10734 and Rule 818.1, Equip is an activated ability. When you activate an equip ability, it is placed on the chain, which provides players an opportunity to respond with [REACTION] cards before it resolves.

The Sequence for Equipping:

Activation: You pay the equip cost and target a unit you control.

Chain Starts: The equip ability is placed on the chain as a pending item.

Priority/Reaction: The game state becomes Closed. Players (starting with your opponent) may now play [REACTION] cards in response to the activation.

Resolution: If the chain resolves and the target remains legal, the gear attaches to the chosen unit.

Important Nuance: As noted in RiftJudge FAQ #634, if an opponent plays a reaction that removes the target unit from the board before the equip ability resolves, the equip ability will fail to resolve because its target is no longer legal.

question: Can I trigger Zhonya's if a unit dies at another battlefield?
answer:
Yes. Zhonya's Hourglass saves a friendly unit regardless of which battlefield it dies at.

Zhonya's says "If a friendly unit would die" — no battlefield restriction. Since it's a replacement effect (not a play ability that targets), it applies to any friendly unit anywhere on the board, whether the unit is at your base, at a different battlefield, or even in combat elsewhere. The battlefield where Zhonya's is placed only matters for where it sits, not for the range of its effect.

question: In reaction to Overzealous Fan dying, can I ambush with Kha'Zix and get the +2 for defending alone?
answer:
Yes, you can ambush with Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror in reaction to Overzealous Fan's ability, and he will successfully receive the +2 Might bonus and 2 XP.

Chain Sequence and Resolution

Overzealous Fan Triggers: When Overzealous Fan is designated as a defender, its ability triggers. Its controller decides to use the ability and pays the cost (killing Overzealous Fan). The ability is placed on the chain as a pending item.

Reaction Window: The chain is now open for you to play Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror as a [Reaction] using the Ambush keyword.

Finalization: You play Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror. The unit enters the battlefield and gains the "Defender" combat designation.

Kha'Zix Triggers: At the exact moment Kha'Zix gains the "Defender" designation, the game evaluates his trigger condition ("if an enemy unit is alone here"). Because Overzealous Fan is no longer present, the enemy battlefield state is considered "alone."

Trigger Placed: Kha'Zix's ability is placed on the chain at the top, above the pending Overzealous Fan ability.

Resolution (LIFO - Last-In, First-Out):

Kha'Zix's ability resolves first. Because the "alone" condition was satisfied at the moment he gained the combat designation, he gains +2 Might and 2 XP.

Next, the Overzealous Fan's ability attempts to resolve.

Key Clarifications

Condition Timing: As confirmed by RiftJudge FAQs #10198, #10735, and #11284, the "alone" condition for Kha'Zix is checked at the exact moment he enters the battlefield and gains the combat designation. The game does not re-evaluate this condition upon resolution.

Chain Placement: By playing Kha'Zix as a reaction to the Overzealous Fan ability, Kha'Zix enters play and his trigger is added to the chain above the Fan's ability, ensuring his ability resolves first.

Note: I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules.

question: If Temporary Leblanc dies and I have no cards in hand, can I use Leblanc legend ability?
answer:
No. The Deceiver legend ability only triggers on Conquer or Hold — a unit dying, even a Temporary LeBlanc copy, does not satisfy that trigger condition.

Even if you were conquering or holding at the same time, you'd still need at least one card in hand to pay the discard cost. Per CR 423.3, discard listed as a cost must be completable to activate the ability, and earlier FAQ rulings (FAQ #10237, #8686, #10107) are clear: with zero cards in hand, you cannot activate Deceiver at all.

question: Does the energy and power resources created by Jhin Murderous Artist when moving disappear at the end of a turn?
answer:
Yes, the energy and power resources created by Jhin, Murderous Artist disappear at the end of your turn.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #4791 and Core Rule 166:

Any energy and power remaining in your resource pool will disappear at the end of your turn (and also at the end of your draw phase).

While the runes that generated these resources remain in their current state (exhausted or ready), the virtual resources themselves are lost.

Jhin's ability simply adds resources to your Rune Pool when you move him; once added, these resources follow the standard rules for resource expiration.

question: Can Charm move something from Vilemaw's Lair?
answer:
Yes, you can target a unit in Vilemaw's Lair with Charm, but the effect depends on where you are trying to move it:

To a different battlefield: Yes, Charm can successfully move a unit from Vilemaw's Lair to another battlefield (RiftJudge FAQ #5028).

To a base: No, you cannot move a unit from Vilemaw's Lair to a base. Vilemaw's Lair contains a "can't" restriction ("Units can't move from here to base"), and in Riftbound, a "can't" restriction always overrides a "can" effect. If you attempt this, the spell will resolve, the unit will remain in the Lair, and the movement portion of the effect will fail (RiftJudge FAQ #9513, FAQ #8797).

Important Note: Even if the movement is prohibited (e.g., trying to move to a base), the unit remains a valid target for the spell (RiftJudge FAQ #5028, FAQ #5698).

question: What resolves first, Guardian Angel or Zhonyas?
answer:
You, the unit's controller, choose which one applies first. Both Guardian Angel and Zhonya's Hourglass are replacement effects that trigger on the same event (the unit would die). Per Rule 372, when multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the owner of the affected object decides the order.

If you choose Guardian Angel first: Guardian Angel is killed instead, the unit is healed/exhausted/recalled to base, and Zhonya's never triggers because the unit never died.

If you choose Zhonya's Hourglass first: the unit is recalled exhausted, Guardian Angel remains equipped to it at base, and GA never triggers because the unit never died.

In both cases, only one gear is sacrificed and the unit is saved. (FAQ #8889, Rule 372)

question: If I Bone Skewer a Ruin Runner does it come in stunned?
answer:
Yes, Bone Skewer can stun a Ruin Runner even though the Ruin Runner has the ability "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities."

According to the official RiftJudge FAQ #8682, a unit's "cannot be chosen" protection ability is only active while the unit is on the board. When the unit is in the opponent's hand, that protection ability is not active, which makes it a legal choice for Bone Skewer.

Sequence of events:

You play Bone Skewer. It resolves, and you choose a battlefield.

Your opponent reveals their hand, and you choose their Ruin Runner.

The opponent plays the Ruin Runner to the chosen battlefield (this is part of the resolution of Bone Skewer).

Because the text of Bone Skewer says "If they do, then do this: [Stun] it," the Ruin Runner is stunned as it enters the board.

Once the Ruin Runner is on the board, its protection ability activates, but it is already too late to prevent the stun from the resolution of the Bone Skewer effect.

question: If you get Switcheroo and have Guardian Angel, when you recall do you go back to normal might or stay at the swapped amount but -1 with the loss of GA?
answer:
You stay at the swapped amount, minus the 1 Might from losing Guardian Angel.

Here's why. Switcheroo calculates the difference between both units' current Might (including all gear bonuses) and applies a fixed +/- modifier for the turn (FAQ #9335). When Guardian Angel triggers, it's killed as part of its replacement effect, so its +1 Might bonus drops off. But the swap modifier from Switcheroo is a layer alteration that persists through the recall — Recalls do not reset Might or remove applied layer effects (CR 455, FAQ #8433).

Concrete example from FAQ #9335: If your unit had 5 Might (base 4 + GA's +1) and Switcheroo swapped it with a 2-Might unit (applying a -3 modifier), your unit sits at 2 after the swap. GA then dies → your unit becomes 1 (2 − 1). After the recall to base, it stays at 1 until the swap effect expires at end of turn.

question: Can you react to triggers during the beginning phase? For example, can a hidden Teemo at a battlefield react to the death of a Sprite Token in order to not be discarded?
answer:
Yes, you can react to triggered abilities during the Beginning Phase, and you can absolutely use a hidden Teemo to save yourself from discarding.

According to Rule 383.3, when a condition for a triggered ability is met, it behaves like an activated ability and is placed on the chain. This means the Temporary keyword, which triggers at the start of your Beginning Phase (Rule 816.1.c), creates a valid window for reactions.

The Sequence

When a Sprite token (which has the Temporary keyword) is at a battlefield with a hidden unit like Teemo, the interaction follows this sequence:

Trigger Phase: At the start of your Beginning Phase, the Temporary ability of the Sprite token triggers.

Chain Starts: The "kill this" trigger goes on the chain.

Reaction Window: You now have an open window to play a [Reaction]. Because playing a hidden card is at reaction speed (Rule 811.6), you can flip your hidden Teemo face-up.

Resolve Reaction: Your Teemo is revealed and enters the board.

Resolve Trigger: With the chain now resolving (LIFO - Last In, First Out), the Sprite's "kill this" trigger resolves. The Sprite token is discarded, but because Teemo is now present at that battlefield, you maintain control of it.

By revealing Teemo in response to the trigger, you ensure you do not lose control of the battlefield, preventing the scenario where you would have been left with no units and thus potentially discarded.

This is based on multiple RiftJudge FAQs (e.g., FAQ #659, #5374) which confirm that Temporary is a triggered ability that uses the chain, allowing you to react by revealing hidden cards.

question: Does Gutter Palace go on the chain? And if so, can you react to it to summon units during the beginning phase?
answer:
Yes, Gutter Palace's "At the start of your Beginning Phase" ability is placed on the chain, and you can react to it.

Does Gutter Palace go on the chain?

Yes. According to Rule 383.3, when a triggered ability's condition is met, it is placed on the chain. Because the ability is placed on the chain, it creates a Closed State, which allows players to play cards or activate abilities with the [Reaction] keyword in response.

Can you react to it to summon units during the beginning phase?

You may activate abilities in response to the Gutter Palace trigger only if they have the [Reaction] keyword or if you have another effect that grants them [Reaction].

Sequence of Events:

Trigger: At the start of your Beginning Phase, if the conditions are met, Gutter Palace’s ability triggers and is placed on the chain.

Closed State: The chain is now active, creating a Closed State.

Reaction: Players may play [Reaction] cards or activate [Reaction] abilities.

Resolution: The chain resolves in reverse order (LIFO - Last In, First Out). If your reaction changes the game state so that the conditions for Gutter Palace are no longer met, the ability will resolve but fail to trigger its effect.

Note: I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules, specifically regarding the conditions for the triggered ability or the specific activated ability of Gutter Palace.

question: Can I use Ahri Inquisitives ability more than once in the same turn if there are multiple showdowns?
answer:
Yes, you can use Ahri, Inquisitive’s "When I attack or defend" ability once per showdown.

According to Rule 383.4.f.2.a and Rule 383.4.e.2.a, "When I attack" and "When I defend" triggered abilities are limited to triggering once per combat. Because per FAQ #6149, you can initiate multiple showdowns at the same battlefield in the same turn, and each showdown constitutes a separate combat, the ability triggers once for each of those combat sessions.

In summary, Ahri, Inquisitive’s ability triggers the first time she gains the attacker or defender designation in each individual showdown.

Note: I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules.

question: If a Recruit token is banished with zero drive, would the zero drive Deathknell re-play it?
answer:
No. A Recruit token banished by Zero Drive's Deathknell cannot be replayed later.

When the token enters the banishment zone, it ceases to exist immediately — tokens cannot exist in any non-board zone (Rule 183.1). By the time you activate Zero Drive's unattached ability to play units banished with it, the token is gone and can't be found or played. This is the same ruling as FAQ #720 for sprite tokens — it applies to all tokens.

question: Can I play Blitzcrank Impassive to an open battlefield?
answer:
No — normally you cannot. An "open" battlefield is uncontrolled and unoccupied (Rule 169.10.c), and you can only play units to your Base or a Battlefield you Control. An open battlefield isn't controlled by anyone, so it's not a valid location to play Blitzcrank to directly.

You can play Blitzcrank to a Battlefield you already control (triggering his ability to hook an enemy over), as confirmed by FAQ #3255. Playing him to an open battlefield requires an external effect like Miss Fortune, Buccaneer that explicitly lets you play a unit to an open battlefield (FAQ #7117).

question: Can you Unyielding Spirit a challenge, or is it not spell nor ability damage?
answer:
Unyielding Spirit cannot prevent damage from a Challenge.

According to multiple RiftJudge FAQs (e.g., FAQ 8394, 4635, 2890), Unyielding Spirit only prevents damage dealt by spells or abilities. Challenge does not deal damage itself; rather, it causes the participating units to deal damage to each other. Because the units themselves are the source of the damage, rather than the spell or ability, this damage bypasses the protection provided by Unyielding Spirit.

question: If someone uses Bullet Time, do they have to recycle Run before I can react?
answer:
No. Your opponent gets to react before you recycle any runes.

Here's the sequence for Bullet Time:

You play it — pay 1 energy, target a battlefield, put it on the chain.

Opponent reacts — they can use Reaction cards or abilities while Bullet Time is on the chain, without knowing how much power you'll spend.

Bullet Time resolves — now you decide how much power to pay by recycling runes, and deal that much damage.

The power payment happens during resolution, not as an additional cost when casting. So your opponent has to make their reaction decision blind — they can't wait to see how many runes you recycle first. If they pass and you start resolving, there's no reaction window after you've paid.

question: If the trigger of frozen fortress is not announced by either players at the beginning phase, will the damage later be applied to the units?
answer:
No, if the Frozen Fortress trigger is not announced and acknowledged by the accountable player, the damage will not be applied to the units.

According to Tournament Rule 506.3, the accountable player must acknowledge their triggers by the time they would have an observable impact on the game. If they do not, the trigger is considered forgotten.

Rule 506.4 explicitly states: "A triggered ability that was forgotten never goes on the chain."

Key Details:

Accountability: As per Tournament Rule 506.1.a, the accountable player for triggers sourced from a battlefield is the player who currently controls that battlefield. If it is uncontrolled, it is the current turn player.

Observable Impact: Dealing 1 damage to units is an effect with an observable impact (as it affects unit health and potential survival).

Result: Once the game has progressed past the point where the damage would have occurred (the Beginning Step) and a new game action is taken, the opportunity to place the Frozen Fortress ability on the chain is lost for that turn. The units will not take the damage later.

If the controller of the battlefield simply missed the trigger, it is treated as a "missed trigger" under the tournament rules (Rule 506.3.b/c). It does not "fire" retroactively later in the turn.

question: If I react to an ability "When you play me" by playing Rengar on the other side, beginning a showdown, does the "When you play me" ability of my opponent resolve before showdown begins or does the chain wait for the showdown to end?
answer:
The "When you play me" resolves first, during the current Chain. The Showdown happens afterward.

Here's why:

Opponent's card is played. If it's a unit, it enters the board at finalization (Rule 337.1.c). The "When you play me" (a Play Effect per Rule 383.4.a) triggers immediately after — becoming a Pending Item on the Chain.

Reaction window opens. After the trigger finalizes, Priority goes to the opponent (controller of the newest item). If they pass, you gain Priority and play Rengar, Pouncing as a Reaction. Rengar is finalized and enters the battlefield — this applies Contested, but the Chain is still resolving so no Cleanup/Showdown happens yet (Rule 321).

The Chain resolves normally (LIFO). Any items added after the "When you play me" trigger resolve first. But once the Chain empties, the "When you play me" — which was already on the Chain from before Rengar entered — resolves. The Showdown is not inserted into the Chain.

Only after the Chain fully empties does the Outstanding Cleanup occur (Rules 319.6, 321.1). That Cleanup stages a Combat at the now-contested battlefield (CR 323.8), and the Showdown begins from a Neutral Open State (CR 323.10–323.12).

In short: the Chain finishes first — including your opponent's "When you play me" — and then the Showdown starts. You can't interrupt a resolving Chain with a Showdown; the Showdown waits for Open State.

question: If you do not control the Abandoned Hall, nor have any units present, and you activate "Ride the Wind" to move a unit to the Abandoned Hall, are you still allowed to trigger the Abandoned Hall to gain +1 might as a spell was played?
answer:
Yes, you are allowed to trigger the Abandoned Hall ability to give your unit +1 [M] (Might) in this scenario.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #11036 and the authoritative interpretation regarding Abandoned Hall (which supersedes earlier, conflicting FAQs), the "When a player plays a spell" ability triggers after the spell has successfully completed its resolution process.

Sequence of Events

Play Spell: You play Ride the Wind as an [Action]. It is placed on the chain.

Resolution: Ride the Wind resolves. Its effect executes: your target unit is moved to the Abandoned Hall and readied.

Trigger Condition Met: Because Ride the Wind has successfully completed its resolution, the "When a player plays a spell" condition on Abandoned Hall is fulfilled.

Trigger Placed: The Abandoned Hall ability is placed on the chain.

Note on Control: As established in the Rules FAQ Clarification 2026-04-29, the player making the choices for a triggered ability of a battlefield (you, in this case, by choosing to resolve the "may" ability) controls that ability and is responsible for adding it to the chain.

Resolution: You resolve the Abandoned Hall trigger. Because your unit was moved to the Abandoned Hall during the resolution of Ride the Wind (which occurred before this trigger was placed on the chain), it is currently at the Abandoned Hall and is a legal target to receive the +1 [M] buff.

Key Clarifications:

Trigger Timing: Triggered abilities that occur when a card is played (such as the one on Abandoned Hall) are placed on the chain only after the spell's resolution process is fully complete.

Targeting: Because the unit arrives at the battlefield before the Abandoned Hall trigger is placed on the chain, it is present on the board when the trigger resolves and is therefore a valid target for the buff.

Control: The fact that you did not control the Abandoned Hall prior to playing the spell does not prevent you from using its triggered ability; by choosing to use the "may" ability, you take control of that instance of the ability.

question: Can you save a unit from dying using Zhonya's Hourglass from a different battlefield than the one the unit is dying on?
answer:
Yes. Zhonya's Hourglass can save a unit on a different battlefield than where it was hidden — the battlefields don't need to match.

Here's why: when played from Hidden, gear is still played to base (not to a battlefield), and Zhonya's replacement effect ("If a friendly unit would die...") doesn't target a unit. Because there's no targeting, the Hidden restriction that limits you to "this battlefield" (CR 811.1.d) never applies. The effect simply looks for any friendly unit about to die, wherever it is.

question: If I'm in control of both battlefields with Ahri Alluring at 5 points, during my beginning phase when I score for holding, does the extra point from Ahri allow me to win the game?
answer:
Yes, you win the game.

You start at 5 points and control both battlefields. During your Beginning Phase, holding the first battlefield scores 1 point (→6), then holding the second scores 1 point (→7). Ahri, Alluring's triggered ability — "When I hold, you score 1 point" — fires from whichever battlefield she's at and scores a 3rd point (→8), immediately winning you the game.

The final-point restriction only applies to conquering (CR 468.1.a.1). Points from other sources like Ahri's triggered ability are not beholden to that restriction and can win the game directly (FAQ #10243, #2646, #1936).

question: If Bloodharbor Ripper returns his only unit at BF with the tap ability, and I react with Rengar Trophy Hunter to it, my Rengar gets played, then his unit gets returned, and then the open showdown starts? Or is it combat showdown, or does the showdown start with still his unit on the board?
answer:
To determine the exact outcome, we must follow the Chain (Last-In, First-Out) and the rules regarding Showdown types and combat staging.

Sequence of Events

Ability Activation: Your opponent activates Bloodharbor Ripper's ability, targeting their only unit at that battlefield. The ability is placed on the Chain. The battlefield is currently controlled by your opponent.

Reaction: You play Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a [Reaction] to the activated ability. Because an enemy unit is present, Rengar's special permission allows you to play him to that battlefield.

Rengar is now added to the top of the Chain.

Chain Resolution (LIFO):

First: Rengar, Trophy Hunter resolves and enters the battlefield.

Second: Bloodharbor Ripper's ability resolves. It returns the opponent's unit to their hand.

State After Resolution: The opponent's unit is gone, and Rengar remains on the battlefield.

Showdown Determination:

Because the battlefield was Contested (you played a unit to a location you don't control), a showdown is staged.

However, since your opponent’s unit was returned to their hand by the Ripper's ability, only your unit remains at the battlefield.

A Combat Showdown is only staged if units controlled by different players are present at the battlefield (CR 323.8, CR 458). Since the opponent has no units there, no combat will occur.

Final Result

Showdown: A Non-Combat Showdown begins.

Conquer: Because only your unit remains at the battlefield, you will establish control (Rule 348.2.a) and successfully conquer the battlefield, provided you have not already scored it this turn.

Summary: Your Rengar arrives, the opponent's unit departs, and you secure the battlefield without combat. You do not have to fight because the opponent's unit is no longer there to contest control.

This is my interpretation based on the mechanics of the Chain (LIFO resolution) and the rules for Establishing Control and Conquering (CR 463.5). No official FAQ exists for this exact combination of Bloodharbor Ripper and Rengar.

question: Can you use Star Spring to bounce Determined Sentry back to base?
answer: No, you cannot. Determined Sentry's static ability — "I can't move to base" — forbids that action, and Rule 054 (Can't beats Can) means restrictions always override permissions. Star Spring's effect trying to move it to base would simply be ignored as an impossible instruction.

question: Can opponent play a reaction spell Flash to me using my Viktor Legend ability?
answer:
Yes, your opponent can play Flash in response to your Viktor Legend's activated ability.

Viktor (Herald of the Arcane) has an activated ability — "1 energy, exhaust: Play a 1 Might Recruit unit token." Activated abilities go on the chain, creating a Closed State where opponents can play Reaction spells (FAQ #4710). Flash has the Reaction keyword, so it can be played in that window.

The sequence works like this: you activate Viktor's ability → it goes on the chain → your opponent can play Flash before it resolves → then Viktor's ability resolves and makes the Recruit token (which itself resolves immediately with no further window).

question: When I play Sacrifice and kill my own Ruined Rex as the additional cost, does the Deathknell ability resolve before or after Sacrifice's draw and channel effect?
answer:
Ruling: The Deathknell ability resolves before Sacrifice's effect. When you kill Ruined Rex as part of Sacrifice's additional cost, the Deathknell trigger becomes a pending chain item that finalizes after Sacrifice finalizes. Because the chain resolves in Last In, First Out (LIFO) order, the Deathknell (newest item) resolves first, dealing 4 damage, then Sacrifice resolves, drawing 2 cards and channeling 1 rune exhausted.

Sequence:

Play Sacrifice and kill Ruined Rex as the additional cost during finalization

Ruined Rex's Deathknell becomes a pending chain item

After Sacrifice becomes a finalized chain item, Deathknell finalizes and is placed on the chain as the newest item

The chain resolves: Deathknell first (deal 4 damage), then Sacrifice (draw 2, channel 1 exhausted)

Nuances:

Pending items finalize up the chain, but finalized items resolve down the chain (newest to oldest)

question: If Sett with a buff gets targeted with Hidden Blade, can he use Sett legend to save him, recall him but still draw 2?
answer:
Yes, you can save the unit and still draw two cards.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #2372 and FAQ #11031, when you use Hidden Blade on a buffed unit and use Sett's (The Boss) legend ability to save it, the draw effect still occurs.

Here is the breakdown of why this works:

Replacement Effect: Sett’s ability is a replacement effect that intercedes during the resolution of the "kill" instruction.

Tracking the Controller: Because the replacement effect only modifies what happens to the unit (recalling it to base instead of sending it to the trash), the unit remains a valid referent for Hidden Blade.

Successful Resolution: Since the unit was a legal target when Hidden Blade began resolving and the controller can still be identified, the draw instruction of the spell successfully executes.

Important Note: The unit must be at a battlefield when Hidden Blade begins resolving for the spell to target it legally. As long as you use Sett's ability during the resolution process to replace the "kill" with a "recall," the controller is still identifiable, and you get your draw.

This interpretation is based on the interaction between replacement effects and spell resolution as described in the FAQ database. No official rule change has altered this interaction.

question: If I score to 8 on my opponent's turn with Thrill of the Hunt, do I win or do I need to conquer both on my opponent's turn?
answer:
To determine if you win the game, we must look at the rules for scoring and the conditions for the "Winning Point."

The Ruling

No, you do not win the game on your opponent’s turn.

According to Rule 323.1 and CR 469, a player wins the game during a cleanup if they have points greater than or equal to the Victory Score and more points than any opponent. While you may reach 8 points through Thrill of the Hunt on your opponent's turn, the game only checks for a winner during a cleanup.

Furthermore, per CR 468.1.b.2, if you are at 7 points and attempt to gain your 8th point (the Winning Point) via a Conquer, you must have scored every battlefield that turn. If you have not scored every battlefield that turn, you will draw a card instead of gaining the point.

Key Clarifications

Conquer vs. Hold: Scoring through Thrill of the Hunt (via conquering a battlefield) is subject to the Winning Point restriction defined in CR 468.1.b.2. This restriction requires you to have scored every battlefield that turn to successfully gain the point.

The "Winning Point" Restriction: The restriction for gaining the 8th point through a "Conquer" is that you must have scored all battlefields in the same turn. If you have only scored one battlefield by conquering on your opponent's turn, you will not gain the 8th point.

Timing: Even if you were to successfully gain the 8th point, the game state is checked for victory during cleanup. Because the turn is still ongoing (it is your opponent's turn), the game will not conclude until the conditions are met and the appropriate cleanup step occurs.

Summary

If you are at 7 points and use Thrill of the Hunt to conquer a battlefield on your opponent's turn, you will draw a card instead of gaining the point, because you have not conquered all battlefields that turn. You cannot win the game by conquering on an opponent's turn unless you have already scored the other battlefield earlier that same turn.

question: If I have equipment attached to a unit already, can I pay the power cost to unequip it from that unit and attach it to a new unit? Neither unit is a weaponmaster.
answer:
No. You cannot pay the Equip cost to reattach an equipment that's already attached to a unit — even to move it to another unit you control.

While equipment is attached, its printed rules text (including the Equip ability) is inactive (Rules 718.2, 135.4). You can't activate an inactive ability. The only way to move already-attached equipment to another unit is via an external effect like Weaponmaster, specific legend abilities (e.g., Jax), or cards like Angle Shot / Relentless Pursuit that explicitly move gear (FAQ 730, FAQ 9593).

If you want to re-use that equipment, you'd need to first get the attached unit killed or otherwise detach the gear (e.g., Strike Down, Veiled Temple), which would recall it to your base — then you could pay its Equip cost fresh during your Main Phase (FAQ 11093).

question: Is activating the list working towards Ezreal Prodigal Explorer draw mechanic?
answer:
No, activating The List does not count toward the activation requirement for your Ezreal legend ability.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #11001:

Ezreal’s legend ability specifically requires that you have chosen enemy units and/or gear twice this turn with spells or unit abilities.

The List is classified as a gear card (Rule 150).

Because there is a formal distinction in Riftbound between unit abilities (Rule 145) and gear abilities (Rule 150), an activated ability originating from a piece of gear does not satisfy the requirement for "unit abilities."

Therefore, even though The List allows you to choose targets when you use its ability, it does not contribute to the "chosen twice" requirement for your Ezreal legend.

question: Can Moonfall select a unit already at a battlefield where your unit is, or no since it's not moving it? Does it still -2 the units?
answer:
No and yes.

You cannot select a unit already at the chosen battlefield for Moonfall's move effect. Moving is defined as a permanent changing from one board location to another (CR 421.1, 441.1). A unit already at that battlefield has nowhere to "move to" — you can't move it to where it already stands. You may choose zero units to move instead.

However, the -2 Might still applies to all enemy units currently at that battlefield, regardless of whether you moved anyone. The second sentence ("Then give enemy units there -2 this turn") is separate from the move instruction and affects whatever enemy units are present at that moment.

question: If I play "call to glory" to buff "unsung hero" can I chain sacrifice so the opponent can't stupefy? If the opponent is able to react with stupefy, can I react with sacrifice, so I'm able to draw anyway?
answer:
Short answer: No to both main scenarios — the timing of the Mighty check blocks both plays. But there's one narrow path that works if your opponent misplays.

Why "chaining Sacrifice right after Call to Glory" doesn't work:

Call to Glory's "+3 might" is its resolution effect — it doesn't apply until Call to Glory resolves from the chain. If you put Sacrifice on the chain above it (so Sacrifice resolves first), Unsung Hero still has base 2 might when you pay Sacrifice's additional cost. Not Mighty — illegal target for Sacrifice. (Rule 357 — costs paid during step 4, before the spell finalizes.)

Why "letting Call to Glory resolve, then Sacrifice" is risky:

Call to Glory resolves → Unsung Hero is 5 might (Mighty). You then play Sacrifice in the Open State. This would work because Sacrifice's cost kills Unsung Hero instantly (step 4), before the opponent can respond (FAQ #9515, #9906).

However, the opponent has a better option: they can respond to Call to Glory while it's still on the chain with Stupefy. That chain resolves LIFO: Stupefy first (-1 might, 2→1), then Call to Glory (+3 might, 1→4). Unsung Hero ends at 4 might — not Mighty. You can never sacrifice it.

If the opponent Stupefies in response to Call to Glory, can you chain Sacrifice anyway?

No. At that point Unsung Hero has 2 might (Call to Glory hasn't resolved). Still not Mighty. Sacrifice has no legal target for its cost.

The one case where you do draw:

If the opponent plays Stupefy after Call to Glory has already resolved (Unsung Hero at 5), you can respond with Sacrifice — kill the Mighty Unsung Hero as cost, draw 2 + channel 1. Then Stupefy fizzles on the missing target but still draws them 1 card (FAQ #10298, Rule 359.3.e.6). But any smart opponent will Stupefy in response to Call to Glory instead, preventing this.

question: If you get Charmed into a battlefield the enemy is defending, who gets priority first?
answer:
When your unit is moved by an opponent's effect (such as Charm) to a battlefield that opponent controls, you become the attacker, and you receive focus and priority first.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #2735 and #8263, when your unit is moved to an opponent's battlefield, that unit applies the "contested" status to the battlefield. Because your unit is the one applying the contested status, you are designated as the attacker, and the attacker receives both focus and priority at the start of a showdown (see CR 461.2.b.1 and CR 461.2.b.1.a).

Key Points on Priority:

Attacker receives priority: Because your unit triggers the contested status, you are the attacker and gain initial priority.

Contested Status: As per Rule 187.3.a.1, units moving to a battlefield apply contested status if the controller of that unit does not currently control that battlefield.

Showdown Flow: The attacker (you) has focus at the start of the showdown, allowing you to start a chain by playing an [ACTION] or [REACTION] card.

Note: While there is some ambiguity in older FAQs (such as #4602) regarding who the game "considers" the initiator, official rulings #2735 and #8263 clarify that the owner of the unit that applies contested status is the attacker and receives focus. I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules.

question: If I attack with a Lonely Poro and it dies in a 2 might to 2 might trade, can I react to the Poro Deathknell to play Nidalee to that battlefield before it dies? (if it was enemy controlled)
answer:
No, you can't play Nidalee there.

Even though Deathknell triggers go on the chain (creating a window to play Reaction cards), Nidalee still follows the normal unit placement rules. Rule 813.3.a is explicit: units with Reaction can only be played to your Base or a battlefield you control. Your attacking Poro was at an enemy-controlled battlefield — you don't control it, so Nidalee can't go there.

Two other things block it too:

Nidalee's Ambush says "to a battlefield where you have units" — your Poro just died, so you have no units there anymore.

The attacking player doesn't gain control until after Conquer resolves post-Combat (CR 466.1.b). Mid-combat, that battlefield isn't yours.

You could play Nidalee to your Base or another battlefield you control while the Poro's Deathknell is on the chain, but not to the enemy's battlefield.

question: If I cast Ride the Wind, and move a unit to Abandoned Hall, does the unit get +1?
answer:
Yes. When you cast Ride the Wind to move a unit to Abandoned Hall, that unit does get +1 [S] from Abandoned Hall's triggered ability.

Here's why the timing works:

Ride the Wind resolves and moves the unit to Abandoned Hall (readying it).

Only after the spell's resolution completes does the "When a player plays a spell" trigger on Abandoned Hall check in. Since your unit arrived during step 1, it is present at Abandoned Hall and is a valid target for the buff.

The trigger goes on the chain and resolves, giving the unit +1 [S].

The key point is that Abandoned Hall's trigger fires after the spell finishes resolving — not while it's still on the chain — so the unit is already there to receive the bonus.

question: If I move into a battlefield with a unit equipped with Eye of the Herald and my opponent reacts with Gust to the move, do I still spawn a recruit?
answer:
No, you will not spawn a Recruit token.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #9629 and FAQ #11340, when a unit equipped with Eye of the Herald moves, its ability triggers and is placed on the chain. If you use Gust in response to that trigger to return the unit to your hand, the unit is no longer on the battlefield when the ability resolves.

Because the ability specifies that the token is played "here," the game must be able to determine the unit's location at the time of resolution. Since the unit is no longer on the board, the location "here" returns "null," and the ability resolves with no effect.

Sequence of Events:

Move: Your unit equipped with Eye of the Herald moves to a battlefield.

Trigger: The Eye of the Herald ability triggers and is placed on the chain.

Reaction: Your opponent plays Gust in response, targeting the unit.

Resolution (LIFO):

Gust resolves first, returning the unit to your hand.

The Eye of the Herald trigger attempts to resolve. It checks for the unit's location to determine where "here" is. Because the unit is no longer on the board, the instruction fails, and no Recruit token is created.

question: Does Arachnoid Horror allow me to play ambush units as reaction speed to a battlefield where there are only enemy units there?
answer:
No. Arachnoid Horror's permission and Ambush's timing do not combine that way.

Ambush (Rule 822.1.b) gives two things: permission to play to a battlefield where you control units, and [Reaction] timing only for that specific play location. The Reaction speed is conditional — it only applies when playing to a battlefield where you already have friendly units.

Arachnoid Horror adds a different permission: you may play to an occupied battlefield where an enemy is alone. But that doesn't give you [Reaction] timing on its own, and it doesn't satisfy Ambush's "where you control units" condition. Since you don't control any units at that battlefield, Ambush's [Reaction] timing is not available.

You could play the Ambush unit to that battlefield during your Main Phase at normal [Action] timing using Arachnoid Horror's permission — but not as a Reaction while the game state is Closed.

question: If my sprite has been dealt 1 damage prior by Frozen Fortress, my opponent attacks me with Stalwart Poro. During the showdown, my opponent plays Discipline and I chain with Stupefy. How does the combat resolve? Please explain the details.
answer:
To resolve this, we must first look at the state of your units and then the combat showdown chain.

Current State

Sprite: Your Sprite is at the battlefield with 1 damage marked on it (from Frozen Fortress). It has 3 Might, meaning it is not yet killed (lethal damage is 3).

Stalwart Poro: As a defender, it gains +1 Might from its Shield keyword, giving it 3 Might total.

Showdown Chain Resolution

Your opponent attacks with Stalwart Poro and plays Discipline (+2 Might). You react with Stupefy (-1 Might).

The Chain (LIFO - Last-In, First-Out):

Top of Chain: Stupefy (yours)

Bottom of Chain: Discipline (opponent's)

Sequence:

Resolution of Stupefy: The spell resolves. Stalwart Poro receives -1 Might. It drops from 3 Might to 2 Might. You draw 1 card.

Resolution of Discipline: The spell resolves. Stalwart Poro receives +2 Might. It increases from 2 Might to 4 Might. Your opponent draws 1 card.

Note: Even though you reduced its Might, the opponent’s Discipline resolves after your Stupefy, so the Poro ends the chain with a higher Might value.

Combat Resolution

After the chain is empty and both players pass, combat resolves in the following steps:

Combat Damage Step:

Stalwart Poro (4 Might) deals 4 damage to your Sprite (3 Might).

Sprite (3 Might) deals 3 damage to Stalwart Poro (4 Might).

Combat Cleanup:

Your Sprite now has 1 damage (from Frozen Fortress) + 4 damage (from Stalwart Poro) = 5 total damage. Since 5 is greater than its 3 Might, your Sprite is killed and sent to your Trash.

Stalwart Poro has 3 damage marked on it. Since its current Might is 4, it survives with 3 damage marked.

Result: Your Sprite is gone. If no other units remain, your opponent has won the showdown.

Disclaimer: This is my interpretation based on the mechanics of the chain and combat rules. No official FAQ exists for this specific chain of interactions.

question: If I singularity a glasc mixologist can the units still be played to that battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can play a unit to that battlefield using the Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell ability after it is killed by Singularity.

According to the RiftJudge FAQ #9329, when Glasc Mixologist is killed by Singularity, its Deathknell trigger is placed on the chain as a pending item before the unit is moved to the trash. Because the game pauses to resolve the chain, you are permitted to play a unit from your trash to that battlefield while the Deathknell ability is resolving.

Sequence of Events

Singularity is played and resolves, dealing 6 damage to Glasc Mixologist.

Glasc Mixologist dies and is sent to the trash.

The Deathknell ability is placed on the chain as a pending item (Rule 322.3).

Players have an opportunity to play [REACTION] cards.

The Deathknell ability resolves, allowing you to play a unit from your trash to the battlefield where Glasc Mixologist died.

Note: This interaction is permissible regardless of whether you have other units at that battlefield or if the battlefield becomes temporarily unoccupied, as the game pauses to resolve the chain items before final cleanup/control checks (Rule 187.4.c, Unleashed Rules Update).

question: Does "when I'm played" trigger when LeBlanc plays her Reflection on a Harness Dragon?
answer:
No. The Reflection token created by LeBlanc's Deceiver legend does not trigger the "When you play me" ability, even if it copies Harnessed Dragon.

There are two reasons. First, the Reflection token is created by Deceiver's ability, not played from your hand — the "play" in Deceiver's text is a token creation effect, not the act of playing a card from hand. Second, the copy effect happens after the token resolves, so the token never has Harnessed Dragon's "When you play me" text at the moment it enters play — that ability is gained later via copying and can't retroactively trigger (FAQ #10386).

question: I move my unit into a bf with my opponent's Fiora Peerless and they have a buff putting them at 4 might. If I play an ambush unit after, would they double the +2 from Yi Legend before my unit is there?
answer:
Yes, Fiora, Peerless will still double her Might if you play an Ambush unit to the battlefield after she has been designated as the lone defender.

According to RiftJudge FAQs (e.g., #11172, #11168, #11396), the "one-on-one" condition for Fiora, Peerless is checked only at the exact moment she is designated as the attacker or defender. Once that condition is met and her triggered ability is placed on the initial chain, her doubling effect is locked in.

The Sequence of Events

Passive Application: As soon as Fiora is designated as the lone defender, the passive ability from Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman immediately applies, increasing her current Might (e.g., 4 base + 2 passive = 6 Might).

Initial Chain: Fiora's "When I defend" trigger is placed on the initial chain.

Reaction: You play your unit with Ambush as a reaction. The game state is now Closed, so this unit is added to the chain above Fiora's trigger.

Resolution (LIFO):

Your Ambush unit enters the battlefield.

The moment your unit enters, Fiora is no longer alone, and the +2 Might passive from Master Yi is removed (per FAQ #11133).

Fiora's doubling trigger resolves. It doubles her current Might at the moment of resolution. Because the passive has been removed, her Might is 4, which doubles to 8.

Post-Resolution: After the trigger resolves, that doubled Might remains for the duration of the combat.

Summary

Because Fiora's ability is a triggered ability that checks its condition at the start of combat, playing an Ambush unit does not cancel the trigger. While your unit's entry will cause Master Yi's passive bonus to "fall off" Fiora immediately, Fiora's trigger will still resolve and double whatever Might she has at that moment.

Note: I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules.

question: Does playing a gold token proc playing a card for Legion effect?
answer:
No. Playing a Gold gear token does not count as playing a card for the Legion condition.

Per Rule 812.1.c, Legion checks whether a card different from the one with Legion has been finalized that turn. Rule 052 defines "card" in game effects as shorthand for "Main Deck card," and tokens explicitly are not cards (Rule 182). A Gold gear token is a token created by an ability, not a Main Deck card — so playing it never satisfies the "played another card" requirement for Legion.

question: Can I play a reaction if I have Vex apathetic on a battlefield and my opponent plays units. Like react to the stun?
answer:
Yes, you can play a Reaction after Vex, Apathetic's trigger is on the chain.

Here's the timing breakdown:

Your opponent plays a unit. As a permanent, it leaves the chain immediately — no response window to the unit being played (FAQ #7795, #5909).

The unit enters the board. Vex, Apathetic's triggered ability condition is met and it goes on the chain as a Pending item.

Now the game is in a Closed State with a pending trigger. During the Execute step of FEPR, players get priority to play Reaction cards or abilities (Rule 813).

So you cannot react before Vex's trigger resolves — there's no window between the unit hitting the board and the trigger firing. But once Vex's trigger is on the chain, you can respond by playing a Reaction spell or activating a Reaction ability (e.g., Flash to save your unit, a pump spell, or anything else with Reaction timing).

Just keep in mind: Vex's stun does not target — it uses programmatic selection (FAQ #9312, Rule 355.10.d). So "can't be targeted" protections won't prevent it, but you can still respond to the trigger itself before it resolves.

question: Can the list card choose the Ruin Runner?
answer:
No, The List cannot choose a Ruin Runner with its activated ability.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #11380, The List’s activated ability requires you to choose a specific unit with the named tag, which counts as targeting that unit. Since Ruin Runner has the ability "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities," an enemy cannot target it with The List's ability.

This interaction is also supported by Rule 355.10, as the ability is not a programmatic selection but rather an active choice made by the player.

question: If I react to Annie readying her 2 runes at the end of turn, by playing Rengar into a battlefield, what happens with the showdown?
answer:
To answer your question, we must look at how the Ending Phase and Showdowns interact.

First, it is important to clarify a timing detail: Runes are readied during the Awaken Phase (at the start of a turn), not at the end of the turn. However, regardless of the timing, if you play Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a [Reaction] to an ability on the chain, the following sequence occurs based on the <showdown_flow>:

1. The Chain Resolves (LIFO)

The Chain is Closed: When you play Rengar, Trophy Hunter, he is added to the top of the chain (he is a unit played as a reaction, so he enters the board at finalization per Rule 359.2.c).

Resolution: Any items added to the chain after the original ability resolve first. Once those are finished, the original ability (the one you reacted to) resolves.

Note: During this time, the state remains Closed. No Showdown can begin yet, because the turn must be in a Neutral Open State to trigger the start of a showdown (Rule 344).

2. Transition to Showdown

Chain Empties: Once the chain is empty and both players pass focus, the game checks the state of the battlefields.

Staging a Showdown: If your move resulted in you playing a unit to a battlefield controlled by your opponent (or an uncontrolled battlefield now occupied by both), the battlefield becomes Contested.

Non-Combat vs. Combat:

If units from both players are present at the contested battlefield, a Combat Showdown is staged (Rule 344.1).

If only your units remain (e.g., if the opponent's unit left), a Non-Combat Showdown occurs (Rule 344.2).

3. Combat or Resolution

If a Combat Showdown is staged, you proceed through the Steps of Combat (Combat Damage Step, then Combat Cleanup/Recall).

If a Non-Combat Showdown is staged, the turn player initiates the showdown, and you establish control of the battlefield if only your units remain (Rule 348.2.a).

Summary

You cannot trigger a Showdown while an ability is still resolving on the chain. You must wait for the chain to fully empty. Once it empties, if the battlefield is Contested, the game will automatically transition into a Showdown (either Combat or Non-Combat) during the next cleanup or state check.
