question: Can you empower renekton any number of time in risen altar
answer:
No — you can't. Risen Altar only discounts actual Empower keyword costs, and Renekton, Brute doesn't have one — and nothing on either card grants the special permission to become Empowered more than once.

Risen Altar reads "[Empower] costs of your units here cost [1] or [A] less." This only reduces costs printed with the Empower keyword (e.g., "Empower [2]"). Renekton, Brute's activated ability is "[1]: Give me +1 Might this turn" — that's a pump ability, not an Empower ability (his Keywords line shows Empowered/Deflect/Ganking only).

Even for units that do have Empower, Rule 827.1.c.1 makes it "Play only if not Empowered." Once a unit gains the Empowered status, the ability can't activate again — unless a card text explicitly grants permission to be Empowered multiple times (CR 442.1.c.1). Risen Altar grants no such permission; it's purely a cost modifier.

Renekton's "When my Might becomes 10 or more, empower me" fires once when he crosses that threshold for the first time (and only if he wasn't already Empowered — "empower me. I become Empowered if I'm not already"). If he's already at 10+, the "become" event never re-occurs (FAQ #11768).

If you disempower Renekton (e.g., with Profiteer), then yes, you could empower him again later — but that's a separate removal/restoration of the status, not "any number of times" from Risen Altar.

question: if I play 2 Deadbloom Predators to the same occupied BF revealed by 2 Dazzling Auroras, do they both participate in the same showdown or do they enter 2 separate showdowns?
answer:
One showdown. Both Deadbloom Predators are controlled by you at the same enemy battlefield, so only one Contested status exists there — that battlefield stages a single Showdown/Combat, and both Deadblooms fight together in it (FAQ #1207; CR 323.7–323.8).

answer:

question: What happen if I cast a targeting spell without paying the deflect cost? Will the spell still go onto the chain?
answer:
No — without paying Deflect, the play is illegal and the spell never becomes a final chain item. Deflect is a mandatory additional cost paid while you finalize the play (choosing targets and paying costs), so a spell that targets a Deflect permanent can't be legally placed on the Chain unless that cost is paid (Rule 809.1.c–d, FAQ #7667).

If you can't pay, the play is undone: the card returns to your hand and it doesn't count as "playing a spell" for triggers. If you merely forgot to pay but a legal alternative target exists, a judge may rewind only the targeting step so you choose a legal target instead of a full undo. Either way, the spell does not sit on the Chain unpaid — Deflect costs aren't applied retroactively, so once it's a finalized chain item it's too late.

question: Can repeat cost be reduced with applied researcher
answer:
Yes — while Applied Researchers is Empowered, its discount reduces a Repeat cost, but only the one you actually choose to pay.

Repeat is an optional additional cost added to the base cost when you declare it (Rule 820.1), and discounts are applied to that combined total once (Rule 356.4.f — same treatment as Eager Apprentice, FAQ #629). So the Empowered discount — spells cost 1 Energy less (minimum 1) and 1 any-domain Power less — shaves the Repeat cost together with the base cost, not twice. If you don't declare Repeat, there's nothing extra to discount; and if the spell's Energy cost is already at the 1 floor, the Energy part of the discount won't help, though a Power-denominated Repeat (e.g. Repeat [A] or [C]) would still get the [A] Power discount.

Her static "Your [Temporary] effects at my battlefield don't trigger" isn't limited to other permanents — it applies to her own source too (same reasoning as FAQ #10040, just with the copy being the LeBlanc itself). So a Reflection copy of her (e.g., from Deceiver) has her passive plus the granted [Temporary], and at the start of your Beginning Phase the kill trigger simply never fires — Rule 816.

Two caveats: the copy must be at a Battlefield — a copy at your Base (e.g., via Mirror Image) isn't "at my battlefield," so it will still die. And this only stops the trigger from firing: if the [Temporary] trigger is already on the Chain when she arrives, her passive won't remove it (FAQ #11578).

question: If Trusty Ramhound is defending at a battlefield with an ally, the ally is assigned lethal damage from the combat resolution, and the Trusty Ramhound is assigned two remaining damage, will Trusty Ramhound live?
answer:
Yes — Trusty Ramhound survives.

Here's why: Trusty Ramhound is Might 3 while its ally is present (base 2 + the +1 Might from its ability). At the combat cleanup's kill check, the game evaluates lethal damage for all units at one point in time while the ally is still alive — so Ramhound has only 2 damage marked against Might 3, which is not lethal. The ally is killed in that same simultaneous event, and then the Combat Special Cleanup's "Heal all Units" step (CR 468.1.a.1) removes Ramhound's 2 damage before any later check can kill it. Even though Ramhound's Might drops to 2 when the ally dies, its damage is already healed.

This matches the established Lee Sin aura rulings (FAQ #5961, #7339) and FAQ #2301: "A unit that would drop to lethal damage after another unit dies will survive if it heals during the cleanup." Note that this only works because healing happens during the same combat cleanup — outside combat (e.g., a kill spell removing the ally), Ramhound would take lethal in the subsequent cleanup.

Combat damage is all dealt at once, and the Combat Cleanup kills lethal-damage units before it heals — but the lethal check happens while the ally is still on the board. Ramhound is at 3 Might (2 base + 1 from the ally), so 2 damage isn't lethal; only the ally dies in the kill step, then Combat Cleanup's "heal all units" removes Ramhound's 2 damage before anything can re-check it (CR 323.4, 468.1.a.1; FAQ #7339/#5961).

A cleaner way to see it: a cleanup can't be interrupted mid-way — nothing between the kill step and the heal step re-evaluates Ramhound's Might. Note the caveat: this survival is specific to combat. If the ally died to spell damage instead, the subsequent non-combat cleanup would have no healing step, and Ramhound would then be killed once its Might dropped to 2 with 2 damage marked (FAQ #7339).

question: In 4 players FFA How meny players can be at the same battlefield while showdown? And how to deal with cards that can create this situation like moonfall and Irresistible Faefolk
answer:
Max is 2 players — combat (and any showdown) only ever involves exactly two players' units in FFA4 (CR 464).

A third player can never have units at the battlefield where a showdown/combat is occurring. That battlefield is an Invalid Destination for their units' moves (CR 449.2.a, 464.1), they can't play units into it (CR 464.2 — they'd go to Base instead), and no unit may move to a battlefield already holding two other players' units "by any means" (CR 451.2). So while other players can cast spells during your showdown (turn order from the attacker), their units cannot be there.

Moonfall and Irresistible Faefolk cannot force a third player into an existing fight. The enemy unit they move is subject to the same destination rules: if it's controlled by a player not involved in the combat who has no units there, the destination is invalid, and the choice itself is "invalid and ineligible to be completed" (CR 464.3). Since both effects are optional ("you may"), you simply move nothing. You can only use them to (a) pull a unit from an enemy who already has units at that battlefield (that unit just becomes the defender), or (b) start a fresh 2-player fight at a battlefield where only you have units — e.g., during someone else's showdown, target a different battlefield you hold; that new fight stages and waits for the current one to finish (FAQ #5108). Moonfall's -2 penalty still hits enemy units there even if you move no one.

question: I attach Shady Spectacles to a non-token unit and make it a copy of Ekko Recurrent. If that unit dies, can I ready my runes if I recicle the unit? While Shady Spectacles is attached, the unit's rules text is replaced by Ekko's (copyable traits), so it dies with Ekko's [Deathknell] — Recycle me to ready your runes and that trigger goes on the Chain normally. This is exactly the flip side of the Reflection token case (FAQ #9947): a token copy of Ekko fails only because tokens cease to exist the moment they hit the trash and there's nothing left to recycle. Shady Spectacles becoming unattached after the unit dies doesn't matter — the trigger and its cost reference the card itself, not the gear.

question: If I move an empowered Akali Deadly Weapon alone into a battlefield, dealing 2 damage to a unit there, and then exhaust Akali legend to pull Akali to base, dealing another 2 damage to that unit, can I respond to the Akali Deadly Weapon's second "when i move" ability trigger and ambush in a Morgana Vindictive to that battlefield as the Akali Leaves, dealing 4 additional damage to that unit and potentially conquering that battlefield with the Morgana?

So at the moment you'd want to play Morgana, you control no units at that battlefield. Ambush only permits playing to "a battlefield where you control Units," and that must hold through finalization (Rules 822.1.b, 822.3). Whether you conquer afterward depends on the enemy unit actually dying from that accumulated damage — a Combat Showdown was initiated, so at its end Combat Cleanup heals all non-lethal damage (FAQ #11658); only lethal damage kills, and if the unit dies Morgana remaining there can establish control and Conquer (assuming you haven't already scored that battlefield this turn, CR 449).

question: Why can nocturne be played when you meet his requirements on an opposing players turn without ambush or reaction but jhin meticulous killer cant not be after also meeting his requirements?

It fires at the exact moment of the look/reveal action, wherever that happens — including mid-resolution of an effect on your opponent's turn — so he doesn't need Reaction or Ambush. He's not a normal "play from hand" at all; the reveal effect essentially embeds permission to play him (to a battlefield you control) right then, with no Reaction window for anyone (FAQ #12292).

Jhin — "If you've spent 4 or more to play a spell this turn, you may play me for [C]." This is a cost replacement, not a timing grant. It changes what you'd pay if you had a legal window to play a unit — but units can only be played in your own Main Phase Open State unless a permissive keyword (Reaction/Ambush) says otherwise. Jhin has neither (his keyword is Vision), so on your opponent's turn you never get a legal moment to play him, and the "this turn" condition lapses at turn's end anyway (FAQ #10443).

Bottom line: Nocturne's ability says "play me now, here's permission"; Jhin's says "here's a discount if the normal timing rules happen to allow you to play me." One opens a window, the other doesn't.

question: Can a 0 might reflection unit (copied something that got star crossed or gust or killed) can conqueer or hold ?

Combat is where 0 Might hurts: if the battlefield it moves to has enemy units, it adds 0 damage and dies to anything assigned to it — conquering only works against empty/uncontested battlefields.

question: Can you chain reactions?
answer:
Yes — you can. Once a chain exists the turn is in a Closed State, and only Reaction-speed cards and abilities can be added to it, so any number of Reactions can stack on top of each other (Rule 309.1.a, 813).

They resolve last-in-first-out, and there's a fresh priority window after each item resolves — both players get a chance to add another Reaction before the next item resolves. So you can keep the chain going at every step, not just at the initial play.

One limit: a Reaction is still a Reaction. You can't slip an Action, a unit, or a non-Reaction activated ability onto an existing chain — wait for it to clear.

question: Define hold
answer:
Hold is the scoring method where a player keeps control: you Hold when you maintain Control of a battlefield you have not yet scored this turn, during your Beginning Phase (CR 471.2). It's the passive counterpart to Conquer — Conquer is gaining Control of a battlefield you didn't control; Hold is still controlling one when your turn begins.

When you Hold, you gain up to 1 point (subject to the Final Point restrictions that apply only to Conquer, CR 473.1.a.1), and any "when I hold / when you hold" abilities trigger at the battlefield that was Held (CR 473.2.b) — these are Hold Effects and go on the Chain as Pending Items. Hold happens as part of the Beginning phase of your turn.

One limit matters in practice: you can only score each battlefield once per turn, so a battlefield you already Conquered this turn can't also be Held for a second point (CR 472).

question: What happens if switcheroo is played on forbidding waste where one player the attacker has a 5 might unit and the other has a 1 might unit defending
answer:
They swap — the attacker's unit becomes 1 Might and the defending unit becomes 5 Might, and Forbidding Waste's -2 keeps applying to the defender on top of that.

Switcheroo swaps the units' current Might (CR 434.1.b: take the difference, increase the lower value and decrease the higher), so the battlefield's -2 is already baked into the defender's 1 when the swap is calculated. The -2 then continues to apply afterward, because Forbidding Waste is a passive "while defending alone" effect that re-evaluates continuously — the defender is still defending alone, so nothing falls off (FAQ #10921).

Practical consequence: since damage uses current Might at the Combat Damage Step (CR 467.2), the 1-Might attacker assigns only 1 damage to the 5-Might defender, while the defender assigns 5 to the attacker's unit — almost certainly killing it. Note the swap only lasts this turn.

question: What's the process of playing a gear, how does equip work, when can I play a gear and equip it, where can the unit be when I equip a gear?
answer:
Short version: Play the gear to your Base (it enters ready), then use its Equip ability — an activated ability usable in your Main Phase during an Open State — to attach it to any unit you control, wherever that unit is.

Playing a gear. Pay its cost; it goes on the Chain, finalizes, and resolves immediately — units and gear skip Execute/Pass, so opponents get no reaction window to the play itself (FAQ #8333). By default gear enters your Base, ready (Rules 149.1–149.2), and can be played on your turn in an Open State.

How Equip works. Equip is an Activated Ability: [Cost]: Attach this gear to a unit you control (Rule 818.1.c.2). It behaves like a spell without a card — it goes on the Chain, so the state closes and opponents can respond with Reactions to it (FAQ #9560). Standard timing is your Main Phase, Open State, and not during a Showdown (Rules 151.2, 381) — so it's neither an Action nor a Reaction (FAQ #1120). Once the gear is attached its rules text goes inactive, so you can't use that Equip ability to move it off (Rules 718.2, FAQ #2139); you can still pile multiple gears on one unit (FAQ #6479).

Timing after playing. Yes — you can play a gear and immediately Equip it in the same Main Phase, as long as you have the resources for the Equip cost and the state is Open with no Showdown running. Quick-Draw is the exception: it grants Reaction inherently and auto-attaches on play (Rule 819.1.d), letting you play and attach at Reaction timing.

Where the unit can be. Anywhere you control it — your Base or a Battlefield you control; Equip has no location restriction on the target unit. If you equip a unit at a battlefield, the gear becomes located there through the Attach action (Rule 152.2); if that unit later dies, the gear stays at that battlefield and gets Recalled to your Base at the next Cleanup (CR 459, 149.3).

question: When Switcheroo swaps current Might values between two units, does the Forbidding Waste penalty get counted once in the swap calculation, or does it apply separately on top of the swapped values?
answer:
Counted once — the −2 is part of the unit's current Might when Switcheroo resolves, and it then keeps applying as an ongoing static effect rather than being added a second time.

Switcheroo determines the difference between the two units' current Might (CR 434.1.b), so Forbidding Waste's −2 is already baked into that number and the swap modifier is sized to hit the correct totals. Unlike a spell effect, Forbidding Waste is a passive "while" ability, so it doesn't snapshot — it re-evaluates continuously (CR 479.4.b, FAQ #10921).

Practical result: after the swap the unit at Forbidding Waste still has the −2 applied on top of the fixed swap modifier. Example — lone defender base 4 (currently 2 with the penalty) swaps with a 6 Might unit: the defender ends at 4 − 2 + 4 = 6 and the other unit at 2. If that defender later stops being alone, the −2 vanishes and it jumps to 8, while the swap modifier stays fixed for the turn.

question: My opponent casts Promising Future, banishing Elder Dragon. I banish Fizz. At which point do I choose the spell Fizz replays? When this happens, can I target his Elder with a Star-Crossed replayed from Fizz?

You pick the trash spell when Fizz's "when you play me" ability is finalized onto the chain — not when Fizz hits the board — and by that point Elder Dragon is already in play, so Star-Crossed can legally choose it.

Here's the flow. And remember, finalize up the chain, resolve down the chain.
Your Fizz enters pending first.
Opponent's Dragon enters pending right after.
Fizz finalizes and resolves, Fizz' 'When you play me' goes as a pending item on the chain.
Dragon finalizes and resolves, Dragon's 'When you play me' goes as a pending item on the chain.
Fizz' ability finalizes -> choice of spell is made here.
Dragon's ability finalizes -> targets are chosen.
Dragon's ability resolves.
Fizz's ability resolves -> the chosen spell becomes a pending chain item.
Finalize the chosen spell -> pick it's targets.
Resolve the spell.

It might very well be that Fizz is already dead by the time your Star-Crossed resolves. But during finalization of Star-Crossed you can pick targets. You need 1 friendly and 1 enemy unit for legal target allocation.

answer:
Nel questo scenario la tua creatura muore senza assegnare i danni perché ogni volta che hai un Combat, la parte prima è un Showdown e solo dopo che chiudete il Showdown potete assegnare i danni.

Allora se nel questo Showdown il tuo avversario gioca Flurry of Blades e questo effetto risolve, ti farà danni primo, c'è un clean up che vede la tua creatura con danni letale e la manda nella tua trash.

Il danno da combattimento si assegna solo nel Combat Damage Step, che si apre dopo che lo Showdown si chiude (cioè dopo che entrambi i giocatori passano Focus in sequenza). Una magia Reaction che risolve durante lo Showdown fa partire un cleanup che uccide le unità con danno letale, quindi l'unità non è più sul campo nel momento dell'assegnazione, e se dell'attacco non resta nessuna unità il Combat Damage Step non avviene proprio (Regola 465.1; FAQ #6476).

L'unico caso in cui la tua unità "muore ma colpisce comunque" è se resta viva fino al Combat Damage Step: lì il danno viene assegnato e poi inflitto simultaneamente, quindi un'unità che riceve danno letale in quel passo infligge lo stesso il suo danno. Quindi: danneggiata ma non uccisa nella Reaction → combatte; uccisa nella Reaction → non combatte.

question:
If I attack with Ezreal Dashing a battlefield occupied by a Scuttle, can opponent react with Rengar Trophy after Scuttle is killed by Ez effet?
And does Ezreal effect trigger again ?
Can he see my hand before deciding to react with Rengar?
And if he reacts to the trigger "When I attack" with Rengar, can I choose him as a target, or I can only select Scuttle?
answer:
Yes on the Rengar window, no on a second trigger.

Rengar's errata'd text ("I can [Ambush] to a battlefield where there are enemy units, even if you don't have units there") lets him be played as a Reaction to that battlefield as long as your Ezreal is still there. So the opponent can respond either while the "When I attack" trigger is still on the chain, or after it resolves and Scuttle dies — the Showdown only closes once all players pass focus in sequence, so they always get a window (Focus stays with you after a trigger chain resolves, Rule 346.1, but you must pass it eventually).

Ezreal will not trigger again. Attack triggers are checked once per combat, when the unit first gains the Attacker designation (Rule 383.4.e.2.a). Rengar arriving mid-combat is just a new Defender in the same combat, not a new combat. (Only if a genuinely separate combat were later staged at that battlefield would Ezreal be the Defender there, and his ability would trigger off defending — once.)

Yes, he can see your hand first. Scuttle Crab's Deathknell is mandatory, so it goes on the chain the moment Scuttle is killed and resolves before the Showdown can close — you're the chosen opponent, so you reveal your hand and the Scuttle's controller may look at your facedown cards this turn. Nothing about that resolution depends on him committing Rengar, so he gets the information before deciding.

Last part: only Scuttle. Targets for a triggered ability are locked in at finalization on the chain (Rule 352.4.b), which happened before Rengar existed at that battlefield, so you cannot point the damage at him — the 3 damage resolves into Scuttle.

question: does star crossed cancel if someone plays temporal breach on a target
answer:
No — Star-Crossed doesn't cancel. It still resolves and returns whichever of its two targets is still legal.

Temporal Breach banishes the unit (moving it to a non-board zone) and then replays it as a new game object, so that unit is no longer the object Star-Crossed chose and becomes an illegal target (Rule 359.3.e.4). But the other target — whichever of the friendly/enemy pair wasn't Breached — is still on the board, and per Rule 359.3.e.8 the spell executes "as much as possible," returning that unit to its owner's hand (FAQ #10821).

One note: because Temporal Breach's unit re-enters as a fresh object, it won't be the one returned to hand even though it's back at the same location.

question: if elder is played from temporal breach and then enemy reacts flash, does that dodge the elder dragon
answer:
Yes — assuming nothing is already damaged lethally, Flash saves the units.

Elder Dragon's "when you play me" ability is a set of location-based targeting restrictions ("up to one enemy unit at each location"), and each target is checked against its own restriction as the ability resolves. Because the Dragon was played via Temporal Breach, it enters and its passive goes active immediately, but its play trigger is placed on the chain after Temporal Breach finishes resolving, so the opponent does get priority and can Flash before the trigger resolves — moving the units to base means they no longer satisfy the restriction for the location they were chosen at, so they take no damage (FAQ 9919).

The one exception: if a unit already has any damage marked on it by Elder Dragon's controller, the passive makes that lethal, and the cleanup before priority is passed kills it before Flash can ever be played (FAQ 12271). Note the moved units don't get picked up by the base instruction — that instruction locked in its own target at finalization.

question: if karthus is killed first in bellows and then 2nd bellows retrigger targets someone else with deathknell does that karthus still proc it
answer:
Yes — the second unit's Deathknell still triggers an extra time.

Bellows Breath's Repeat executes the whole effect a second time during the same resolution (Rule 820.1.d), and Bellows Breath resolves fully before any cleanup. Karthus has lethal damage marked but hasn't been moved to the trash yet, so he's still on the board and his passive ("Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time") is still applying when the second unit's Deathknell trigger is created. In fact it would work even if both deaths were truly simultaneous (FAQ #10742 / #5353) — passive abilities don't need to survive their own death.

The contrast case: if Karthus had been killed and trashed by a separate, earlier spell or ability (with a cleanup already resolved in between), his passive is gone and the later Deathknell would only trigger once. New choices for the repeated execution — including a different unit — are legal (Rule 820.2.a).

question: If akali moves to a BF and does 2 dmg. then leaves and does 2dmg. but it does not kill the unit. does the unit heal?
answer:
Yes — the unit heals, because a Combat Showdown was opened.

Since there was an enemy unit at that battlefield, Akali's arrival staged a Combat Showdown, and Combat Cleanup heals all Units in play regardless of whether the damage was lethal or whether the unit actually fought (CR 468.1.a). Akali's "When I move" damage is just marked damage, not a kill — so it gets wiped at the end of that combat unless it killed the unit. Pulling her back with Rogue Assassin doesn't dodge this: the legend can only be activated at Action speed, meaning the Showdown is already running and will still clean up (FAQ #11658, #11899).

The one exception is if she's pulled out before the Showdown ever opens — i.e. moving her back at Reaction speed in response to her own move trigger while the chain is still non-empty (like a Flash), so no Combat was ever staged. In that case no Combat Cleanup occurs and the 4 damage stays marked (FAQ #11658). With the legend, that window doesn't exist.

answer:
No — the unit doesn't heal, as long as the pull-out happened before an actual Combat Showdown opened.

This is the classic Akali pattern: you move her in, hold her "When I move" trigger on the Chain, and reaction-speed move her back out (e.g. Flash). Because no item-free Cleanup ever occurred with you still present, the Combat Showdown never opens — Contested just gets removed in Cleanup (CR 323.10), so there's no Combat Cleanup and therefore no healing. Both 1-damage triggers resolve and the damage sticks (FAQ 11658).

The distinction that matters: healing only happens during Combat Cleanup after a Combat Showdown (CR 468.1.a.1) or at the end of the turn (Rule 317.2.b). If a Combat Showdown did open — say you used the Rogue Assassin legend at Action speed while a combat was already running — then Combat Cleanup would heal the surviving unit back to full unless the damage was lethal.

question: Can I use fiora worthy ability in an active showdown
answer:
Yes — but only if its trigger condition happens during that showdown.

Fiora, Worthy's "When a unit you control becomes [Mighty], you may pay [C] to ready it" is a triggered ability, not an activated one, so it isn't blocked by the rule that keeps regular activated abilities out of showdowns (Rule 145.2, 381). When a unit you control actually becomes Mighty (hits 5+ Might, including from a mid-showdown buff or a defender's +1), the ability goes on the chain and can be responded to; the [C] is paid as it resolves, and the ready happens then. If nobody became Mighty — for example Fiora was already Mighty before the showdown started — there's no trigger to use.

See FAQ 6927 for the same sequence: a unit becomes Mighty mid-showdown, Fiora's ability is used, cost paid, unit readied.

question: Can i use trigger ability in a showdown?
answer:
Yes — triggered abilities aren't "activated," so they work during a showdown. A trigger fires automatically when its condition is met and goes on the chain as a Pending Item, and Rule 383.3.c allows that during Closed or Open states on any player's turn, showdown or not.

The key distinction is what the ability is. If it starts with "When…", "At…", or "The Nth time…", it's a triggered ability and it triggers during a showdown just fine. If it's written as [Cost]: [Effect], that's an activated ability, and by default it can only be used on your turn, in a Neutral Open state, out of showdown (Rule 381) — so it can't be used in a showdown unless the card grants it Action or Reaction.

One caveat: if a spell you want to play in response has to be Reaction once the trigger starts a chain — a trigger that opens a chain puts the state in Showdown Closed, where only Reaction-speed plays are legal.

question: Can i use trigger ability's multiple times
answer:
It depends on the trigger — triggered abilities are by definition repeatable, but several things cap them.

Normally a triggered ability fires every time its condition is met (Rule 383), so if the condition genuinely happens twice, you get the effect twice. But watch these caps: abilities that say "once each turn" or "the first time…" only fire that many times (Rule 383.3.e), Attack and Defend triggers only fire once per combat even if the unit gains the designation again in that same combat (Rules 383.4.e.2.a / 383.4.f.2.a), and Conquer triggers need an actual Conquer — since each battlefield can only be scored once per turn, you can't re-conquer it to farm the trigger.

question: Can i use trigger ability's multiple times? Like Fiora worthy
answer:
Yes — triggered abilities have no once-per-turn limit unless the card says so. Fiora, Worthy just repeats: "When a unit you control becomes [Mighty], you may pay [C] to ready it" — every time a unit makes that transition (Might going from under 5 to 5+), a fresh instance goes on the chain with its own [C] payment.

Note you're not "activating" it on demand — you only get a trigger each time the condition is actually met. If a unit drops below Mighty and then climbs back (spending a buff and regaining it, for example), that's a new transition and Fiora triggers again; same if several units become Mighty at once, in which case you get one instance per unit and choose their order (Rule 383.3.d).

The ability also won't trigger off a unit that enters play already at 5+ Might — there has to be a real change while it's in play. Limits like "once each turn" or "the first time" only apply when the text includes them (Rule 383.3.e), and Fiora, Worthy has no such wording.

question: Can I move irresistable faefolk targeting akali deadly weapon, then ambush in a unit in response to akali deadly weapon's damage before my faefolk dies?
answer:
Yes — you get that window. Akali's "When I move" trigger is placed on the Chain after Faefolk's own move-trigger resolves, and the damage isn't dealt until that trigger resolves. Nothing is marked on Faefolk yet, so you control a unit at that battlefield and can play an Ambush unit there as a Reaction (Rules 822.1.b, 383.2.c).

Two things to keep in mind. First, Akali's target is locked in at finalization before you ambush, so if she chose the Faefolk that damage still lands on resolution — your ambush doesn't redirect it. Second, the ambush must be a genuine Ambush (or otherwise grant Reaction/permission for that location); without it a plain Reaction unit can't be played into a contested battlefield (Rule 813.3.a).

And to be clear about the timing you're asking for: the Faefolk does die. It only dies in the Cleanup after the Chain empties, once the 1–2 damage is actually marked (it's a 1-Might unit, so either value is lethal). So yes, the ambush resolves and enters before Faefolk dies — the Faefolk just won't survive the cleanup.

question: Can I use Fiora worthy ability in combat?
answer:
Yes — Fiora, Worthy's ability is a triggered ability ("When a unit you control becomes [Mighty]…"), so it can go on the chain during a Combat Showdown.

The Main Phase / Open State restriction (Rule 381) applies only to activated abilities. Triggered abilities fire whenever their condition is met, including mid-combat — e.g., a unit reaching 5 Might from a buff, a Might pump, or Shield kicking in when it's declared as a defender. Resolving it during combat is fine; you just pay the [C] and ready the unit.

Two caveats: the trigger only sees an actual in-play Might change to 5+, so a unit that enters play already at 5+ Might won't trigger it (Rule 709 / FAQ #5835); and like any trigger it uses the chain, so opponents get priority in response.

question:
If I have a void hatchling on the board and play double trouble or ivern which say:
look at the top 3 cards you may reveal a unit...

Does the void hatching trigger at all?
answer:
Short answer: Void Hatchling doesn't "trigger" at all — it's a replacement effect, not a triggered ability — and it hooks onto the reveal part of Double Trouble / Ivern, Nurturer, not the "look at the top 3."

The look-at-3 is a look, not a reveal, so Hatchling has nothing to apply to there — same reasoning as Stacked Deck (FAQ #1404). But both of those cards then instruct you to reveal a unit from your deck, and that's the instruction Hatchling replaces: you look at the top card of your deck first (which will be one of the three you're already looking at), you may recycle it, and then you reveal a unit from among the looked-at cards and draw it.

Practically, that's a small upgrade — you get to bottom the top card before making your choice instead of having it swept up in "recycle the rest" afterward — and note if you recycle the card that was your unit, it's gone before the reveal happens.

One caveat: FAQ #766/#1404 establish the look-vs-reveal split and that Hatchling replaces rather than triggers, but I didn't find a published Q&A that runs it against Double Trouble/Ivern specifically; the above is the Rek'Sai precedent (FAQ #315) applied to these cards.

question: When opponent's warwick enter and I have emperor divide in hand. Can I use emperor divide from my hand to escape warwick kill ability?
answer:
No — not from hand. Emperor's Divide in hand is only an [Action] spell, and once Warwick's attack trigger goes on the chain the turn is in a Closed State, where only [Reaction] cards can be played (Rule 309.1.a). Warwick's "when I attack, kill all damaged enemy units here" trigger is added to the initial chain of combat, so your only window there is reaction speed.

Note there's also no window earlier: playing Warwick gives no reaction opportunity (permanents auto-resolve), and he's already an attacker with the trigger on the chain by the time a showdown opens, so you never get an Open State to play the Action before the kill resolves.

If you had hidden Emperor's Divide earlier at a battlefield you control, it would work — from Hidden it gains Reaction and plays for [0], so you could respond, moving your damaged units to Base; they're no longer "here" when Warwick's trigger resolves and so survive (same logic as FAQ #3645).

Flash in response: still no damage. Flash sends her back to base and adds a second "When I move" trigger (the battlefield she moved from), but the Chain never empties, so no Showdown ever opens and Akali, Silent never gains a designation — neither trigger can choose her. question: If a flow card is in trash, and you conquer with Kennen, can I play using kennen’s flow cost instead?
answer:
Yes — you choose. Both the printed Flow cost and Kennen's granted Flow cost become instances of Flow on the same spell, and the controller picks which one to apply when playing it (Rule 829.1.c.3).

Worth knowing: Kennen's granted cost is "equal to its cost," which is checked against the spell's printed cost (CR 206) — so it's usually the base cost, and for most Flow spells (e.g. Shadow Dash at [5][A][A]) Kennen's grant is the cheaper option. You're never forced to use it; if the printed Flow cost is lower, take that one.

Two timing notes: the grant only lasts that turn, and Kennen's "When I conquer" trigger resolves as the showdown closes/control is established, so there's no showdown window left at that instant (FAQ #12519) — you need a later legal window that same turn (a Showdown for an Action spell, or any priority if the spell has Reaction if these happen on your opponents turn or during your turn when the turn is in the Neutral Open state, which is when no Chain exists and there is no Showdown active). question: When Kennen, Keeper of Balance is played from Ava Achiever's ability, does Kennen's ability trigger twice, from being played and from attacking?
answer:
Yes — you get two separate instances of the ability, one for each condition met.

Kennen's "When you play me or I attack" is a single triggered ability but with two distinct trigger events, and it has no "once each turn" limit, so each fulfilled condition puts its own instance on the chain. The "when you play me" instance is placed when Kennen enters (Rule 383.4.a.2); because Ava plays him "here" into the battlefield where her combat is ongoing, he then gains the Attacker designation during the next Cleanup along with his controller (Rule 323.2.a), which places the attack-trigger instance (Rule 383.4.e.2). Arriving late to a combat still counts — that's the same principle as FAQ #4095/#716.

Each instance is a separate "you may pay [2] to stun a unit," so you decide independently for each: pay for one, both, or neither, and you choose the order if they're placed simultaneously (Rule 383.3.d). Note Ava plays him from hand, not from Hidden, so neither stun is restricted to targeting units at his battlefield. If he's played somewhere he never becomes an attacker (e.g.: base, if Ava's moved to base before her trigger resolves), you get only the single play trigger.

question: How would this interaction work if I had a Viktor, Leader on the board? Because Patched Porobot is both a gear and a unit would killing it trigger Viktor, Leader and let me play a Recruit unit token?

Yes — Viktor, Leader triggers and you get a 1 Might Recruit token.

Patched Porobot is both a Unit and a Gear, and per the multiple-types rules it keeps all the properties of both (Rule 178.1). Jayce's "kill a friendly gear" instruction resolves and sends Porobot to the trash from the board — that's a kill, so the permanent's death is a unit's death. Since Porobot is a non-Recruit unit you control, Viktor's "when another non-Recruit unit you control dies" condition is satisfied, and Viktor is still on the board to see it (no simultaneity problem here, unlike Viktor dying alongside another unit).

Timing: Viktor's trigger is placed on the chain as a pending item while Jayce's play effect is resolving, so it finalizes and resolves after Jayce's ability finishes — you play the Recruit token into your base, and you can still play the gear from hand any time later that turn (per the Jayce clarification).

question: does killing a gold gear token activate the sivir battle mistress legend ability?
answer:
No. Sivir, Battle Mistress (Battle Mistress) has exactly two triggers: "When you recycle a rune, you may exhaust me to play a Gold gear token exhausted" and "When one or more enemy units die, ready me." Killing a Gold gear token satisfies neither.

A Gold token is a gear, not a unit (Rule 187.5), so its death never counts as "an enemy unit dies." And killing a gear is not recycling a rune — recycling is a specific action that moves a rune back into your rune deck, not a Kill (CR 429). Note also that when you kill the Gold via its own ability ("Kill this, [E]: [Add] [A]"), the kill is a cost, not a recycle, so nothing about that sequence touches Sivir.

So the only ways to fire Sivir are a genuine rune recycle (for the Gold token trigger) or an enemy unit actually dying (for the ready trigger).

question: After playing a unit with Glasc Mixologist Deathknell, does the HP reset?
answer:
Yes — the unit you play from the trash enters with no damage marked on it, and any damage on your surviving units was already healed before the trigger resolved.

Damage doesn't persist on cards in the trash, so the new unit enters fresh. And in the standard case (Mixologist dying in a Combat Showdown), Combat Cleanup heals every unit in play before the Deathknell trigger is finalized and resolved, so you can't use the trigger to "finish off" an enemy that survived combat — they're already healed to full by the time your unit arrives (CR 463.1.a.1). This is also why Mixologist's Deathknell can't save a unit that already took lethal damage.

One caveat: the automatic heal only comes from Combat Cleanup (or the end-of-turn heal). If Mixologist is killed outside combat, nothing is auto-healed — but the newly played unit still enters with zero damage either way.

question: Can I star Crossed a sprite token in the beginning phase by reacting to its own temporary trigger?
answer:
Yes, the timing works — but Star-Crossed needs two targets, so it often can't be cast at all in that spot.

Temporary is a triggered ability that goes on the chain at the start of its controller's Beginning Phase, which creates a Closed State, and Star-Crossed's [Reaction] lets you play it there (Rules 816, 813). Confirmed by FAQ #6571/#5523, which allow reacting to a Sprite's Temporary trigger. However, Star-Crossed requires both a friendly unit and an enemy unit as targets — if the Sprite is your only unit, or your opponent controls no units, you have no legal cast.

Note that bouncing your own Sprite doesn't save it: the token goes to hand and immediately ceases to exist (Rule 186.1), so it leaves play just the same. The difference is it isn't "Killed" — so any Kill/Deathknell-style triggers won't fire, and the Temporary trigger resolves afterward with nothing left to kill.

question: Are there are Order or Law cards that allows me to play cards more than once, from the grave, or send back to my hand
answer:
Yes, but not many — and there's no "Law" domain in Riftbound (the domains are Order, Chaos, Calm, Body, Mind, Fury; "Keeper of Law" is simply an Order card).

For playing out of the trash, Order has Spectral Matron, Glasc Mixologist (on Deathknell), and the spell Undying Loyalty — each plays a unit from your trash ignoring its cost. Order also carries the Flow keyword (Dragon Form, Lacerate, Shadow Dash, Public Execution, Lightning Rush); Flow is a permission plus alternate cost that lets you play that same spell from your trash once, then it's banished — that's the main "play a card more than once" mechanic in these colors.

For returning cards to hand, Starhound is the only Order hit, and it's narrow: it returns a Bird, Cat, Dog, or Poro from your trash to hand. Order has no board-to-hand bounce, and Forge of the Future recycles up to 4 cards from trashes back into the deck (not your hand). Nothing in Order (or anywhere) loops a card back repeatedly for free.

And the showdown ended with no unit died, and the Apprentice was sent back to the base. He then attacked with the Ravenbloom student. What should be the might of my Poro at this point?
answer:
Your Poro is 2 Might when it defends against the Ravenbloom Student.

The key is what Smoke Screen saw when it resolved. By then the Apprentice had already moved in and the combat showdown had started, so your Poro was the lone defender and Wuju Bladesman's "defending alone" passive was live — its Might was 2 + 2 = 4. Smoke Screen's -4 is clamped by its "minimum of 1" clause and snapshots at that moment, so it locks in as -3 for the turn, not -4 (CR 479.4.b; increases apply before decreases, FAQ #1455).

After that: Discipline +2, then Stupefy -1 (applied unclamped, since the Poro was at 3 then). So when the Student attacks: 2 base + 2 (defending alone) − 3 (Smoke Screen) + 2 (Discipline) − 1 (Stupefy) = 2 Might.

Worth flagging the trap: if you'd let Smoke Screen resolve before the Apprentice moved (as in the classic Watcher/Stalwart Poro line), it would have snapshotted at only -1 and your Poro would be 4 here. Because it resolved mid-showdown, you take the -3.

question: all types of chain?
answer:
There's only one Chain — Riftbound doesn't have "types" of chains. Rule 330.1: only one Chain can exist at a time, and any new card or ability played while it exists gets added to that same chain (330.2).

What does have categories is the items on it. Every chain item is either Pending or Finalized: it's added as a Pending Item and becomes Finalized after the Check Legality step of playing it (Rule 329). Items that can sit on the chain are cards (units, gear, spells), tokens, and abilities — activated, triggered, and reflexive (CR 328.1, 389).

One practical split worth knowing: permanents (units and non-unit gear) leave the chain when finalized and hit the board immediately (Rule 359.2), while spells linger on the chain as Finalized items until they resolve (359.3). Everything resolves last-in-first-out (Rule 340.1).

question: What opens a chain outside and inside of showdowns?
answer:
One thing opens a chain everywhere: an item becoming Pending. Three sources — playing a card, activating an ability, or a triggered ability becoming Pending (CR 328, 402.1). When it isn't your turn you would need a triggered ability or a showdown to be able to start a chain; only one chain exists at a time, so "starting a chain" only applies when no chain exists yet (Rule 330).

Outside a showdown (Neutral Open): the default opener is the turn player in their Main Phase, playing a card or activating an ability. Note the state immediately becomes Closed once that happens, so follow-ups need Reaction. Triggered abilities can add items in any state, on anyone's turn.

Inside a showdown: the player with Focus may start a chain with a card or activated ability that is legally timed — during Showdown Open that means Action or Reaction by default; nothing else is playable (Rule 347.1). Each spell played this way creates a chain as normal (Rule 342.1), and once a chain exists only Reactions can be added. Triggered abilities still land on the chain (e.g. attacker/defender triggers form the Combat Chain when combat opens).

One subtlety: a Reaction can be the first item of a chain, since Reaction grants all Action permissions plus Closed-State play.

question: what are the steps of a chain in and outside of a showdown
answer:
Same four steps either way — the FEPR loop (Finalize → Execute → Pass → Resolve, Rules 337–340). Only the permissions and what happens when the chain empties differ.

Finalize: each controller completes the play steps for their Pending items in the order they were added; units, gear, and Add-resource abilities resolve immediately on finalizing (337.2). Execute: the player with Priority (in a showdown, the player with Focus) plays a legally timed card/ability or passes — in a Closed State outside a showdown that means Reaction only, while in a Showdown Closed state an Action card that opened the chain is also fine (338.1.a.2, 358.4). Pass: if everyone passes in sequence without adding anything, go to Resolve; otherwise priority moves to the next player in turn order. Resolve: the newest item resolves fully (LIFO), then back to Finalize if the chain isn't empty, or the turn returns to an Open State if it is.

The real divergence is after that last resolution: during a showdown, Focus passes to the next player in turn order (340.2.a) — except when the chain was opened by a triggered ability or an Add ability, in which case the player whose Focus it was, will keep Focus (346.1). Outside a showdown there's no Focus at all; the turn simply returns to Neutral Open and, after any cleanup, the Turn Player gets priority back in their Main Phase.

question: can a token exist without its owner card. for example zed making a shadow token
answer:
Yes — tokens don't need any owner card to exist. Tokens are their own category of Game Object, not cards (Rule 185), so a Shadow Clone created by Zed, Without a Sound exists on the board purely as a token.

Its "owner" is just defined as whoever controlled the effect that created it (Rule 183), which is Zed's controller — no physical card is required or tracked. The token persists on its own even if Zed later leaves play; the only thing that makes it vanish is being put into a non-board zone other than the Chain (Rule 186.1), e.g. if it's killed into the trash. So a token can't "exist" in your hand, deck, or trash, but on the board it's a fully independent object.

question: Complete list of everything that can be reacted to
answer:
Short answer: you can react to anything that stays on the Chain as a finalized item. Reaction isn't about "responding" to arbitrary events — it's a permission to play/activate during a Closed State, so a window only exists if something is sitting on the chain.

Reactable:

Spells — they linger on the chain after finalizing (Rule 359.3), so opponents get priority before resolution.

Triggered abilities of any sort — "When you play me," "When I attack/defend," "When I move," Deathknell, reflexive triggers, etc. (Rule 383).

Activated abilities, including Equip and any gear/unit/legend ability with [Reaction][>] or [Action][>] (Rule 818.1). Reactions can also stack on other Reactions.

Any of the above during a Combat Showdown, as well as combat triggers like "When I attack."

Not reactable:

Playing a unit or gear — permanents leave the chain the moment they finalize, so no window exists (Rule 359.2). You can react to any "When you play me" trigger the permanent creates.

Hiding a card — discretionary, no chain.

Discretionary actions that don't use the chain: Standard Move, Recalls, scoring/Conquer/Hold, combat damage, cleanup steps (FAQ #5996, #2835).

Add abilities and tapping runes for mana — these finalize and resolve immediately, even mid-resolution, so nothing lingers to respond to (CR 430.2, FAQ #3799).

One practical note: Reaction isn't strictly "responding." On your own turn you can play a Reaction with an empty chain just like an Action spell; it's only priority that limits you on an opponent's turn (FAQ #11498).

question: Can battlefield triggers be reacted to?
answer:
Yes — battlefield triggered abilities go on the Chain like any other triggered ability, and once an item is on the Chain the state is Closed, so players may respond with Reactions (Rule 383.3, 813.1.c).

The catch is that there must actually be a trigger to respond to. Battlefield abilities only trigger when their condition is genuinely met — e.g. a Hold ability only fires if a unit was present at that battlefield when its controller scored the point, so with no units there and no Hold, nothing goes on the Chain and there's no window (FAQ #10348). Also remember triggered-ability targets are locked at finalization, so you can react, but you can't react to a trigger and then have a newly revealed unit become its target.

question: Can I react to shens “when I hold with one other unit I score” or any passive type abilities
answer:
Yes for Shen's hold ability — no for genuine passive abilities.

Shen, Leader of the Kinkou Order reads "[Shield] When I hold, if there is exactly one other unit you control here, you score 1 point." The "when I hold" clause makes this a Hold Effect, i.e. a triggered ability, so it's put on the chain as a pending item and every player gets a Reaction window before it resolves (Rule 383.4.d). What you can't react to is the hold/score event that caused it.

One nuance: the "exactly one other unit you control here" clause sits immediately after the trigger condition, so it's part of the condition, not the effect (Rule 383.2.a.1) — it's checked when the trigger fires, and killing that other unit in response won't stop the point. Once the trigger is on the chain it resolves.

Passive abilities are different: they're statements of fact with no "when/at" condition (Shield is a passive, for example), they never use the chain, and there is no priority window in which to react to them — they just continuously apply.

question: When a spell played with flow is countered, does it get banished instead of going to the trash?

Being countered is exactly that kind of departure, so the trash destination is replaced by banishment — this is an explicit exception to the normal countered-spell rule (CR 426.1.a.1). The same holds if the counter effect would otherwise return it to hand, e.g. Abandon (FAQ #11738).

Note the distinction: this only applies to the Flow play. A copy of that same spell played from hand for its normal cost and countered just goes to the trash.

answer:

One caveat: this only works if the +5 is on the unit receiving the Spectacles. If it's the copied unit that's big only because of a temporary buff or its own gear, none of that transfers — the copy takes printed/copied traits only (FAQ #12291).

answer:
No — not with the opponent controlling Promising Future. Flurry is played second, so it's the newest chain item and resolves first (LIFO, Rule 340.1). Switcheroo swaps current values (CR 434.1.b): the difference is 2, so the lower unit (Tideturner, 0) gains +2 and the higher (Pit Rookie, 2) loses 2. Forbidding Waste is a "while" static effect that keeps re-applying, so Tideturner ends at 2 + 2 (swap) − 2 (penalty) = 2, and Pit Rookie at 2 − 2 = 0 (FAQ #12532).

question: Can a Champion Legend be played?
answer:
No — a Champion Legend is never "played." It's established at the start of the game: each player places their Champion Legend in the Legend Zone during setup, and it stays there for the duration of regular play (Rules 174.2.a–174.2.b, 111).

Everything it does, it does from that zone. Legends can have Passive, Triggered, and Activated abilities, can be targeted by spells and game effects, and can't be Killed or Moved (Rules 174.3–174.8). Note that non-Champion legends added by other effects are a separate case — they aren't Champion Legends and can leave the Legend Zone (Rule 107.4.d.2).

question: can you react to astral heron trigger, can you play a reaction speed card between 2 heron triggers on Bfs assuming they both flat the trigger already
answer:
It depends which "between" you mean — you cannot insert a Reaction between the two Herons triggering, but you can play one between their resolutions.

Both Herons trigger simultaneously when you play your first card, so they go on the chain together as pending items, with you choosing their order (Rule 383.3.d). Finalizing doesn't pass priority (Rule 337.1.a), so there's no window to act until all pending items are done — the opponent can't slip a Reaction in ahead of the second trigger being queued.

Once the first Heron trigger resolves, though, priority goes to the controller of the next item on the chain (Rule 340.4), so you get a genuine window before the second trigger resolves. The chain is non-empty there, so it's a Closed State: only Reaction cards/abilities are legal.

One real consequence: a card played in that window is "the next card you play this turn," so it would consume the first Heron's discount, leaving the second Heron's discount for the card after that — you'd have to actually want that. If your goal is stacking both discounts on one card, just pass and let both triggers resolve (FAQ #11679).

question: i have heron and thousand tail watcher on a battlefield, my opponent uses rampage paying its additional cost targetting his empowered ambessa, the wolf, and my heron, i play from hidden temporal breach targetting my thousand tail watcher to reduce the might of his units, can i play a spell later with the reduction from heron?

1 - Unit: Thousand-Tailed Watcher (pending)

Chain:
2 - Heron trigger (pending)
3 - Watcher trigger (pending)

We finalize 2, the Heron trigger resolves and gives the discount to the next card played after that.
We finalize 3, Watcher reduces the Might of all opposing units (this turn).

question: How is cauculated the Split damage from Alpha strike
answer:
Split damage from Alpha Strike is calculated at resolution, not when you play it.

At finalization you choose the friendly unit and the targets — you can pick at most as many enemy units as that unit's Might at that moment (Rule 355.14.c). When the spell actually resolves, you take the chosen unit's current Might (including any buffs granted in the meantime), then divide that total among the locked-in targets, choosing the split at that point (Rule 355.14.e). Each target must get at least 1, so if the Might dropped between finalization and resolution and there's now more targets than damage, you choose which targets cease being targets — but you can't leave fewer targets than you have damage to divide (Rule 355.14.h).

Bonus damage (e.g. from Annie, Fiery) adds to the total before you split it, not +1 per target (Rule 715.3).

question: heal after showdown
answer:
It depends on whether the showdown was a combat showdown — those heal all units; non-combat showdowns heal nothing.

If units controlled by different players were both present (a real combat), the Combat Cleanup during the Resolution Step heals all damage off every unit in play at once — including units sitting at Base or at other battlefields that never fought (CR 468.1.a.1, 463). But a non-combat showdown (you move to a battlefield and no enemy units are there) has no combat damage step and no Combat Cleanup, so damaged units just stay damaged (FAQ #9726, #11213).

answer:
Yes — the trigger can be used on your opponent's turn, because Deceiver is a triggered ability: triggered abilities can be put on the chain during Closed or Open States on any player's turn (Rule 383.3.c). Rule 381's "your turn only" restriction applies to activated abilities, not triggers.

The catch is the condition still has to actually happen. Two cost notes: "discard 1 and exhaust me" is a cost, so you need a card in hand and LeBlanc must be ready. Her trigger still goes on the chain while she's exhausted (FAQ #604), but you can't finalize it if you can't pay the exhaust (CR 415.4, 423.3). The catch is Repulse's own target: it must choose a friendly unit at a battlefield. Harnessed Dragon has no location restriction and can kill a unit sitting in your Base (FAQ #5926), and in that case you can't legally play Repulse at all — the ability still resolves.

question:
If units have already damage on them from a spell, and also no showdown takes place to heal them. Then opponent plays elder, do the damaged units die immediatly from elder static ("any damage is enough to kill units") ?

answer:
Yes — the pre-existing damage matters, and those units die the moment Elder Dragon hits the board (provided that damage was dealt by Elder Dragon's controller).

Elder Dragon's static doesn't deal damage; it redefines lethal damage for units carrying damage marked by its controller, so any non-zero amount is lethal (CR 142.4.c, 323.4). Spell damage stays marked until the end of turn — it only heals after combat or during the end-of-turn cleanup — so it's still sitting there when the Dragon enters, and a cleanup runs before anyone gets priority to react to the "when you play me" trigger (FAQ 10686, FAQ 11876). No showdown or combat in between makes no difference; if anything, it just means nothing healed the damage away.

The one real condition: "your damage" is relative to the Dragon's controller. If the earlier spell was cast by the Dragon player's opponent, that damage is not theirs, and the passive won't make it lethal.

question: assume i have a zhonyas hidden, my opponent hollows breath's that battlefield and then plays elder. Do i have a window to play the zhonya's? If so, can my opponent target the saved unit with elder's ability afterwards
answer:
Yes, you get the window.

Facedown cards have Reaction, so you flip Zhonya's in reaction to Bellows Breath while it's on the chain. Zhonya's is a gear permanent, so it resolves immediately and its replacement effect is live before Bellow Breath resolves; when Bellow Breath would kill your unit, Zhonya's kills itself instead, and the unit is healed, exhausted, and recalled to Base (Rule 369). If it doesn't kill your unit, damage just stays marked.

Afterwards, yes — your opponent can absolutely target the saved unit with Elder Dragon. Elder's play effect chooses "up to one enemy unit at each location," and your Base is one of those locations, so the recalled unit is a legal choice there. Because Elder's passive makes any of its controller's damage lethal, the 1 damage kills it, and Zhonya's is already used up (it died as its own replacement cost). Nothing about the save grants protection.

If your unit would have survived the Bellows Breath and have the 1 damage still marked, it would die when Elder Dragon enters play. Since Elder Dragon entered play, it's 'when you play me' ability is added as pending to the chain and since Elder Dragon left the chain we run a cleanup. In this cleanup your unit dies due to Elder Dragons passive and still having 1 damage marked from the opponents Bellows Breath. If you played your Zhonya's in reaction to Bellows' breath, it saves your unit and recalls it healed to base. Now we finalize the Elder Dragon 'when you play me' ability. Your saved unit now in base can be chosen as a target at a location. Your base is a legal location.

If you however did not play it before that and all your units at battlefields are killed, you will still have a window when Elder Dragon's When you play me ability goes on the chain. It's not an optional triggered ability so it will go on the chain, its controller has to finalize it. Afterwards because the chain is still not empty at this point, you can play your zhonya's and potentially save a unit in another location or just save your gear from being trashed.

The location trick only works in the other order: if Elder's play effect has already locked in the unit at the battlefield and you recall it before that ability resolves, it stops fulfilling the targeting restriction and is unaffected (2026-04-29 Elder Dragon clarification). Once it's sitting at Base before Elder is played, it's fair game.

Note: I couldn't find a card named "Hollow Breath" in the database — if it's a spell that deals damage/kills at that battlefield, the ruling above holds as written.

If a chain is currently open at all, it's only for resolving new things — the killed unit is already in the trash, and Janna's heal only touches units on the board, so it can't bring it back. answer:

question: how burn out works
answer:
Burn Out is a forced replacement effect that happens when you try to move more cards out of your Main Deck than are actually in it (CR 432).

The sequence is: do as much of the action as possible, Recycle your Trash into your Main Deck (randomized), choose an opponent to gain 1 point, then finish the rest of the instruction. So if you're told to Draw 4 with 3 cards left, you draw 3, shuffle your trash back in, then draw the 4th — you don't burn out mid-draw (CR 414.4, FAQ #3374). Same for Burning/trashing cards: burn what you can, burn out, then burn the rest.

Only actions that actually move cards out of the deck cause it. Looking at or Revealing cards in excess of your deck size does not burn you out — the cards are still in the Main Deck zone while revealed (CR 432.1.c, FAQ #5695).

If your deck and Trash are both empty, you burn out repeatedly, one point to an opponent each time, and after the first Burn Out those points can't be replaced or prevented. Points gained this way can be the winning point — they aren't restricted like Conquer or Hold — and the win happens immediately if it pushes someone past the Victory Score with more points than everyone else (CR 432.3.c.1).

question: What happens to a player in FFA when they attempt to draw from an empty deck?
answer:
They Burn Out. They draw as many as possible (none), recycle their trash into their Main Deck (randomized), choose an opponent to gain 1 point, then finish the draw instruction (CR 432.2).

In FFA the only difference from 1v1 is that "choose an opponent" is a real choice among multiple opponents — you pick who gets the point. If the deck and trash are both empty, you'll Burn Out repeatedly, handing out 1 point each time until an opponent reaches the Victory Score (8 in FFA3/FFA4) and wins (CR 432.3).

Note that points from Burn Out aren't subject to the final-point restriction that applies to Conquer, so a Burn Out point can win the game at match point (FAQ 7293).

Two caveats: she still only stuns one unit, not the whole battlefield (FAQ #10205), and she must be alive and still at that battlefield when the trigger resolves, since "here" is checked on execution (FAQ #10045). question: LeBlanc, Deceiver interaction with gusting. If I react to the initial trigger and gust all valid targets, what happens? If I react to the reflexive trigger and gust the chosen target, what happens?
answer:
Reacting to the initial "when you conquer or hold" trigger cannot stop the token. That trigger targets nothing — LeBlanc's controller already paid the discard/exhaust costs at finalization — so Gusting the units there only strips away the copy candidates. However, when attempting to finalize the reflexive trigger in the chain, because there isn't any valid target it is removed from the chain and never finalized (See #388.1/#402.4). Therefore, since the token was never given temporary, what remains is a plain 0 [M] reflection token.

Reacting to the reflexive trigger is the cleaner line: Gust resolves first (LIFO), sending the already-chosen copy target to hand — a non-board zone, which severs the targeting relationship — so the copy instruction mistargets and does nothing, per Rule 359.3.e.7. The token is already on the board as a 0 [M] unit and keeps its granted Temporary, so it dies at the start of its controller's next Beginning Phase, before scoring.

If you'd rather kill the token outright, Gust it instead in that second window — it's a legal target while still 0 [M], and a token sent to hand ceases to exist, leaving nothing to copy and no Temporary to matter.

question: Can a teammate invite another teammate to play ambush unit in a state?
answer:
No — the 2v2 invitation only lets you play spells and activate abilities on your teammate's turn, not play units, so an Ambush unit can't be played off an invitation in an open state (CR 491.8.a; FAQ #3647 lists spells and abilities only, explicitly excluding units and gear).

question: how does diana lunari work? do you check and recycle optionally before reveal?
answer:
Yes — you Predict first (look at the top card and optionally Recycle it), and only then does the reveal happen.

Full sequence: when a showdown begins at Diana's battlefield, her triggered ability goes on the chain. On finalization you may pay [1]; the payment is optional, and per the Vendetta rules update you can decline even if you have Energy floating (CR 445.2). If you pay, you [Predict] — look at the top card of your Main Deck and choose whether or not to Recycle it (CR 437.1). If you Recycle it, it goes to the bottom and the "reveal the top card" then shows the new top card; if you don't Recycle, you reveal the card you just looked at. If the revealed card is a spell, you draw it. It's a single dig — no repeated Predict.

Two things people get wrong: the Predict look is private while the reveal is public (opponent sees that card), and declining the [1] means the whole thing is skipped, including the reveal — the reveal is part of the paid effect. Note the trigger fires off any showdown at that battlefield, including a non-combat showdown from moving onto an empty battlefield (FAQ #9373), and it still resolves even if Diana is removed after the trigger is on the chain (FAQ #10222).

question:
how does astral heron work for a chain when playing your first card. what counts as the first card played in this example:

You play temporal breach, they counter with repulse, you defy it, they play another repulse targeting breach.

So repulse2 resolves, defy resolves, repulse1 gets countered, temporal breach gets countered.

answer:
Yes — "your first card played" is determined by which card finishes resolving first, not by chain order, hand order, or how many cards got countered along the way.

In your stack the items resolve newest-first: Repulse 2 → Defy → Repulse 1 → Temporal Breach. Defy sits above Breach, so Defy resolves first, and that's the first card you played this turn — Heron triggers then (as long as Heron is at a battlefield at that moment, per Rule 383.2.a.1) and your next card this turn costs [2][A][A] less. Breach never counts: a countered card isn't considered played at all (CR 420.4.a.1 / 425.1.b), and it resolves last anyway. Same answer for your second question — if you stack 3 Reactions, the last one you played resolves first, so a card that was third out of your hand can absolutely be your first card played, while the two beneath it (if countered) never count.

Two limits worth remembering: Heron triggers only once per turn and only off the first card that resolves, and the discount must be used this turn (it expires in the Expiration Step).

question: how does the end turn phase work. when it goes to other player whats the rule , also how many cards do you draw at the very start of the game
answer:
The Ending Phase is the two-step wrap-up of your turn (Rule 317).

Ending Step — "at the end of the turn" effects fire here. Abilities like Annie's or Dazzling Aurora's triggers go on the Chain and resolve through normal FEPR, so opponents can respond with Reactions only because a Chain exists — not because the phase changed.

Expiration Step — an Ending Special Cleanup runs, inserting: all units heal all damage, all "this turn" effects expire simultaneously, and every player's Rune Pool empties (unspent Energy and Power are lost). If any items went through FEPR during this step (e.g. a trigger fired), you loop back to the start of the Expiration Step and do it again (317.2.f). Once clean, the next player in the turn queue becomes the Turn Player.

One quirk worth knowing: that heal is global — every unit in play heals, including ones at Base that never fought. Also, since the Expiration Step loops, damage dealt by a trigger resolving there doesn't carry into the next turn.

question: If a glasc mixologist dies in the beggining phase, can the unit generated by its deathknell hold that battlefield and therefore score to 8?

Yes — provided the death happens before your Beginning Phase's Scoring Step.

The Beginning Phase is a Beginning Step followed by a Scoring Step that Holds every battlefield you control (CR 315.2.b, 471.2). If Glasc Mixologist dies during that Beginning Step — say, to a start-of-phase trigger or a spell played in an Open state before the step resolves — its Deathknell goes on the chain as a Pending Item before it hits the trash, and because an item is on the chain you can't lose control of the battlefield in the meantime (same reasoning as FAQ #9149). You resolve the Deathknell, play the unit to that battlefield you control, and it's still there when the Scoring Step runs — so you Hold and gain the point.

That point can absolutely be the eighth: the Final Point restriction in CR 473.1.b applies only to points gained through Conquer, and points from other sources aren't beholden to it.

question: If Diana Lunari is dealt lethal damage by a Shurkien Flip and an empowered Akali Deadly weapon moving into that battlefield, can I still trigger Diana Lunari's ability?
answer:
No — Diana's ability won't trigger, because she's dead before the Showdown actually begins.

Her trigger checks "when a showdown begins here," and by the time the Combat Showdown opens, she's no longer at that battlefield. Moving is instantaneous, and Akali's "When I move" trigger is placed on the chain and fully resolves before any showdown can start — a Combat/Showdown only begins in a Cleanup with an empty chain, and showdowns/combats are staged and opened at the very end of the cleanup (CR 323.7–323.12, 462). So Shuriken Flip's 2 damage resolves, then Akali's move trigger adds 2 more, and Diana (3 Might) dies during the cleanup at step 3b — which runs before Step 9/10 begins the Showdown/Combat (CR 323.4).

By the time the Showdown begins she has already left the battlefield, so the "when a showdown begins here" condition can't be evaluated for her (Rule 383.2.c.2). This is different from removal after the fact: if her trigger were already on the chain, it would resolve independently of her (FAQ #10222) — but here it never gets placed at all. Note also that the Akali trigger damage is what makes the damage lethal; either way it resolves pre-showdown, and if Diana were the only opposing unit, that battlefield becomes a Non-Combat Showdown.

question: I have a unit at 0 or even negative might. When this turn ends, will it be granted any status or keyword like "temporary" that will kill it next turn? Or is its might return to normal when the turn ends?
answer:
No. Being at 0 or negative Might doesn't grant any status or keyword — Temporary only applies if a card actually gave the unit Temporary (Rule 816); having low Might never creates it.

At the end of the turn the Expiration Step heals all units and expires every "this turn" effect simultaneously, so the Might modifiers fall off and the unit goes back to its printed/base Might plus any persistent modifiers (attached Gear bonuses, passive abilities) — Rule 317.2.

Also worth separating: 0-or-less Might is never itself lethal. The unit only dies if it has non-zero damage equal to or exceeding its Might (CR 143.2.b), so a 0-Might unit with no damage simply survives the turn.

The one case where it does die next turn is if it genuinely has Temporary (e.g., a Sprite token) — that trigger kills it at the start of its controller's Beginning Phase before scoring, independent of its Might.

question: If an Athakan is played onto a battlefield and I have an Overzealous Fan there, can I bounce the Athakan back without triggering its attack ability?
answer:
No — you can't stop the attack trigger from triggering, but your bounce can make it resolve for nothing.

Playing Atakhan into a battlefield you don't control applies Contested, and since your Fan is sitting there, that stages a Combat. When combat opens, Atakhan is established as the Attacker and its "When I attack" trigger is put on the chain as part of that same combat-opening step (CR 466.2.c–e) — before any player has a chance to play or activate anything, so there's no window to bounce it first. Your Fan's defend trigger activates at that same moment (it gains the Defender designation) and is placed on the chain after the attacker's, so it resolves first (LIFO) — you kill the Fan as the ability's cost and move Atakhan to base.

The trigger itself is already on the chain and still resolves, but by then "here" no longer refers to that battlefield, so the instruction can't be carried out and nothing gets killed — exactly the Fight or Flight example in Rule 359.3.f.2 (attacking unit moved to base in reaction, attack trigger mistargets). Note the Fan still dies as the cost either way, and you must choose Atakhan as the target when you finalize the ability.

question: In 2v2 mode (Magma Chamber), the opponent moves in to fight my ally at a battlefield they control. Can I play Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a reaction to help defend my ally?
answer:
No — Rengar can't be played to that battlefield to help your ally.

Combat can only ever occur between units controlled by exactly two players (CR 464), and a battlefield with a Staged Combat or Combat in Progress is an invalid destination for a unit controlled by anyone who isn't already a participant — by any means, including Ambush (CR 464.2). Once the opponent's unit moves in against your teammate's unit, those two players are the combatants; you're a third player, so Rengar has no legal landing spot there. Rengar's expanded Ambush permission ("even if you don't have units there") only widens which battlefields are normally valid — it doesn't override the multi-player combat restriction, and if an effect forced a unit there anyway it would be played to your Base instead (CR 464.2.a).

Note that a "friendly/teammate" designation doesn't change this — combat still counts distinct players, and your teammate's Defenders don't become yours. You can still play the Rengar itself during the turn (just to your Base or a battlefield you legally control), and you're free to help your ally with Reaction spells/abilities, since teammates can be invited to play cards with priority (CR 491.8.a).

question: if you play ruined rex. then target it with baited hook. it dies and you choose a target for its deathknell before you draw for baited hook correct? and in which case its on the chain. if your baited hook gives you karthus is that ruined rex 4 damage now doubled? does it double the chain item or double the amount of times it goes on chain?

question: Does baited hook kill friendly unit part of finalization or resolution

What happens at finalization is only the choose/target step — you pick which friendly unit to kill when the ability is placed on the chain, which is why opponents get a Reaction window before the kill actually occurs.

Practically: if the chosen unit is removed or bounced in response, nothing gets killed, the "killed unit" reference is null, and you look at 5 cards but can't play any of them. question: how can you allocate dmg. can i spread out 7 dmg to 7 diff units even if none will die
answer:
No — you can't spread damage freely. Combat damage is assigned one unit at a time, and each unit must receive lethal damage in full (non-zero damage equal to or exceeding its Might) before you assign any damage to the next unit (CR 467.2.c.3).

So with 7 damage you'd kill at most two units (3 + 3, with 1 left over to a third) if the units have 3 Might, not sprinkle 1 on seven units. You also can't over-assign: a unit can't receive more than the minimum lethal amount unless no further units remain to receive damage (CR 467.2.c.4) — that's the only case where the leftover lands all on one unit.

Two exceptions worth knowing: a unit that can't be dealt damage at all (e.g., damage fully prevented or "I don't take damage") is exempt from the mandatory-assignment math (465.2.c.10), and effects that redefine lethal — like Elder Dragon's "any amount of your damage is enough to kill enemy units" — let you assign just 1 to each unit and move on. Tank/Backline shift who gets assigned damage first, but never let you skip the lethal-in-full requirement.
